name: Counter-Strike 2

validation.notes: Built from the game files (build of 22 Oct 2026) and research. HUD positions are estimates from the layout files and were not checked against live captures; the recogniser reads what it can and leaves the rest out. With Game State Integration on, rounds, money and your kills and deaths come straight from the game.

capture.notes: Fullscreen windowed or borderless capture works best. For the death map, set the radar to fixed: Settings > Game > Radar / Tablet > Radar Is Rotating: No, and keep Radar Centers The Player: Yes. Turn on Game State Integration in Settings > Game data for exact rounds, money, kills and deaths.

modes.label: Your own server with bots only

playerContext.label: Your radar
playerContext.help: With a fixed radar (Radar Is Rotating: No, Radar Centers The Player: Yes) the coach stitches each map from it and pins where you die and where killers were to the spot; with a rotating one, only to the callout.

playerContext.label: Your usual role (optional)
playerContext.help: Lets the coach judge deaths against the job: an entry is meant to die first sometimes, a support or anchor should not.

vision.purpose: Counter-Strike 2 (Premier, Competitive, Wingman, Casual, Deathmatch or Practice). Read the round score at the top centre (CT score left of the round timer, T score right) and which side the player is on, the players alive on each side, the round timer or the bomb icon, the player's money, health and weapon, the place name under the radar (top left) and the map and mode. Detect the player's own death (death panel 'killed you with their …', freeze-cam on the killer, the spectator view of a teammate) and own kills (kill-feed entries with a red outline and the player's name on the left), and the round end banner. Read the fight from the player's own view, the kill feed, the death panel and the radar. Enemies are only known where the radar or the view shows them (red dots: spotted); never guess hidden enemies. Give unknown for anything not clearly visible.

state.label: Rounds won (your team)
state.description: Rounds won by the player's team: the number beside the round timer on the player's side (CT left, T right). Omit if you cannot tell the player's side.

state.label: Rounds won (enemy)
state.description: Rounds won by the enemy team, the other number beside the round timer.

state.label: Your side
state.description: The player's side: Counter-Terrorist (blue HUD and avatars) or Terrorist (gold). From the HUD colour, the team avatars or the buy menu.

state.label: Round time left (s)
state.description: The round timer (m:ss) converted to seconds. Omit when the bomb icon has replaced it.

state.label: Bomb planted
state.description: True when the round timer is replaced by the red bomb icon (planted).

state.label: Your team alive
state.description: Players alive on the player's team, from the team counter at the top (avatars not greyed out).

state.label: Enemies alive
state.description: Players alive on the enemy team, from the team counter at the top.

state.label: Money
state.description: The player's money ('$1,234') at the bottom left, above health and armour.

state.label: Health
state.description: The player's health number at the bottom left (cross icon).

state.label: Kills
state.description: The player's kills, only from the scoreboard (Tab) or the end-of-match screen.

state.label: Deaths
state.description: The player's deaths, only from the scoreboard or the end-of-match screen.

state.label: ADR
state.description: The player's average damage per round, only from the scoreboard or end screen.

state.label: Map
state.description: The map name from the loading screen, the scoreboard header or the map pick, as one of the names in the Game reference (e.g. Mirage, Dust II).

state.label: Mode
state.description: The game mode (Premier, Competitive, Wingman, Casual, Deathmatch…) from the loading screen or scoreboard.

state.label: Your weapon
state.description: The weapon the player holds, from the bottom-right weapon panel or the view model, using the Arsenal names exactly (e.g. 'AK-47', 'AWP'). Omit if not visible.

state.label: Where you are
state.description: Where the player is now, as one callout name from this map's list in the Game reference. The white place name under the radar names the game's own area (e.g. 'BombsiteA', 'Long Doors'): give the matching callout from the list. Not while spectating a teammate after death.

state.label: Your height
state.description: The player's own level on Nuke (upper: A and Outside; lower: B, Ramp's bottom, Secret, Decon): from the view and the radar's level. Omit if unsure or on other maps.

state.label: Where the killer was
state.description: Right after the player's death: the callout the killer was in, from the freeze-cam view of the killer's surroundings or the killer's red dot on the radar. Omit otherwise.

state.label: Killer's weapon
state.description: On the death panel ('<name> killed you with their <weapon>') or the kill feed: the weapon's Arsenal name. Omit otherwise.

state.label: Spotted enemies
state.description: Callouts where enemies are visible now (on screen, or red dots on the radar), as 'count Callout', comma-separated, e.g. '2 Long Doors, Mid'. Never guess unspotted enemies; omit if none.

events.label: You died
events.description: The player's own death: the death panel ('<name> killed you with their <weapon>', 'You were killed by the C4 explosion'), the freeze-cam turning to the killer, or the kill feed entry with the player's name on the right and a dark red background. Not a teammate's death.

attributes.description: The death panel says who killed you and with what: "<name> killed you with their <weapon>", or "You were killed by the C4 explosion", "You burned to death", "You were killed by your own grenade". The kill feed shows the same weapon icon between the two names.

Read the kill feed (top right) for 5 seconds after your death. Your death entry has a dark red background. If a later entry shows one of your teammates (your team colour: CT blue, T gold) killing the player who killed you within 5 seconds, the death was traded. The 5-second window is the common…

From your own view in the last two seconds before death: count enemy players visible on screen or firing at you (muzzle flashes, tracers from different directions), and red enemy dots near you on the radar (top left). Two or more separate sources of fire, or a second kill-feed name hitting you in…

From your view: the scenery still sliding sideways or forwards and the weapon bobbing when you fire means moving; a sudden rise and fall of the view means a jump; a lowered camera means crouching. The kill feed shows an in-air icon when the killer was airborne. With Game State Integration or…

Your screen turns white (or partly white) after a flashbang goes off and fades over a few seconds. If that white-out is present at the moment of death, you were blind. The kill feed also shows a flashbang icon and an assister name (Attacker + flash icon + Assister) when an enemy teammate flashed…
The kill feed shows a smoke cloud icon after the weapon icon when the kill passed through a smoke. On your own view a grey smoke cloud sits between you and the killer.

The kill feed shows a penetration (wallbang) icon after the weapon icon when the bullet passed through cover. On your view you were hit while the killer was not visible. Leetify data show wallbang kills in about 40 percent of matches for an average player, so a repeated spot matters more than a…
The kill feed shows the headshot icon just before the victim name when the final hit was to the head. Your own kills read the same way, and the scoreboard HS% column gives the match share.

Estimate from your view: the size of the killer model on screen (a head several crosshair gaps wide is close; a head smaller than the crosshair centre is long), or from your position and the killer's red dot on the radar. Distance bands are coaching rules of thumb, not game values.

At the moment of death, read the radar (top left): your own arrow and your teammates' coloured dots. No teammate dot within a short swing (roughly one room or one corner away) means you were alone. After death the camera moves to spectate a teammate, so read the radar from the last frames before…

The first kill-feed entry of a round is the opening duel. If your name is the victim in that first entry (dark red background), it was an opening death; if you are the killer (red outline), an opening kill. The team counter at the top of the HUD drops from 5 to 4 at the same moment.

In the 3 seconds before the duel: a flash, smoke, molotov or HE thrown by you (throw animation, grenade leaving the HUD inventory) or by a teammate (grenade arc and detonation near the fight). No friendly grenade going off near the fight means no utility.

From your view and HUD: moving out from cover towards an angle means peeking; standing still aimed at an angle means holding; moving across an open lane means crossing; the reload animation or a 0 on the ammo counter means reloading; the defuse progress bar on screen means defusing; the planting…

Your buy from the HUD (primary weapon, armour icon, grenades) or the scoreboard money and equipment; the enemy buy from the killer's weapon in the kill feed and death panel (a pistol or SMG while you hold a rifle suggests an eco). Game State Integration reports money and equipment value for the…
The team counter at the top centre of the HUD shows each team's players alive (avatars, or numbers if the Large Player Count option is on). Compare the two counts in the last frame before death.

events.label: Bomb planted
events.description: The round timer is replaced by the red bomb icon, or "The bomb has been planted" is announced.

events.label: Bomb defused
events.description: The defused-bomb icon or "The bomb has been defused" banner.

zones.label: Radar area
zones.description: Divide the map into a 3x3 grid, north up as on the game's overview. Use the callout's grid cell from this map's list, or the player's arrow on a fixed radar. If neither is clear, give no zone.

concepts.title: Numbers decide rounds
concepts.summary: Each death turns a 5v5 into a 5v4, and the team with the opening kill wins about two rounds in three (SCOPE.GG 2026). Most coaching points come back to keeping your numbers: trade deaths, avoid lone fights and do not give away free kills.
good: Trading every opening death
Playing tighter when ahead on players
bad: Lone peeks in a man advantage
Early, untraded deaths

concepts.title: Stop to shoot
concepts.summary: CS2 punishes moving shots: a rifle is many times less accurate while moving. Every duel is won by stopping first, with the crosshair already at head height.
good: Counter-strafe, then shoot
Crosshair at head level before the peek
bad: Running and shooting
Jumping shots with a rifle

concepts.title: Placement beats reaction
concepts.summary: Good crosshair placement means the enemy walks into your aim. It shortens time to damage more than faster reactions do and is the habit coaches check first.
good: Pre-aiming the common spot
Small, controlled adjustments
bad: Big flicks to every enemy
Crosshair on the floor while moving

concepts.title: Information is currency
concepts.summary: Knowing where the enemy is, how many and with what lets the team make the right call. Collect it cheaply (jiggles, sound, utility), share it in short calls, and do not die for it.
good: Short, clear calls after contact
Using a jiggle or a molotov to learn the count
bad: Dying for information nobody hears
Silent contacts

concepts.title: Utility first, then aim
concepts.summary: Smokes, flashes, molotovs and HEs win fights before the bullets: they remove angles, blind defenders and push players out of spots. A team that uses utility together takes fights on its own terms.
good: Flash before every contested swing
Grouped utility on executes and retakes
bad: Dying with grenades in your inventory
Utility thrown alone and early

concepts.title: Economy is a team resource
concepts.summary: Money is shared through drops and through timing. The team buys, saves and forces together, plans two rounds ahead with the loss bonus, and keeps weapons alive when a round is lost.
good: Same buy across the team
Saving a lost round to keep rifles
bad: Mixed buys
Throwing away the AWP in a hopeless round

concepts.title: The clock is a weapon
concepts.summary: CTs win if time runs out; Ts win if the bomb explodes. The side with time on its side should wait and make the other side come. Every decision, from the default to the clutch, should account for the clock.
good: CTs delaying with utility
Ts holding post-plant angles instead of hunting
bad: CTs peeking when the clock favours them
Ts walking onto a site with 10 seconds left

concepts.title: One angle at a time
concepts.summary: A duel against one player is fair; a duel against two is usually lost. Clear angles one by one, set up crossfires as a defender and isolate fights in clutches.
good: Slicing corners from cover
Crossfires that make attackers face two ways
bad: Standing where three angles can see you
Peeking two enemies at once

concepts.title: Predictable is punishable
concepts.summary: Opponents learn your habits quickly. The same spot, the same timing and the same re-peek get pre-aimed. Vary positions, timings and utility, and move after every contact.
good: Changing position after a kill
Mixing off-angles with standard spots
bad: Re-peeking the same angle
Holding the same spot every round

concepts.title: The bomb changes who must move
concepts.summary: Before the plant, attackers must come to the defenders. After the plant, the defenders must come to the attackers. Good post-plants and retakes come from understanding this switch.
good: Ts waiting for the defuse after the plant
CTs grouping before the retake
bad: Ts peeking after the plant
CTs retaking one by one

concepts.title: Play your role
concepts.summary: Entry, support, lurker, anchor, AWP and IGL have different jobs and different stat lines. Judge a game by what the role needed, not only by the kill count.
good: Support players with high flash assists
Anchors who delay and survive
bad: Everyone playing as the entry
The lurker joining the execute late

concepts.title: Deaths tell patterns
concepts.summary: One death is noise; ten deaths are a pattern. Group deaths by what the screen showed: moving or still, traded or not, flashed or not, alone or with a teammate, and fix the most common avoidable one first.
good: Reviewing deaths after each match
Working on one habit at a time
bad: Blaming luck
Trying to fix everything at once

concepts.title: Lost rounds still matter
concepts.summary: A round that cannot be won can still be used: saving weapons, dealing damage for the next round, or delaying the enemy economy. Treat each round as part of the half, not on its own.
good: Saving rifles in hopeless rounds
Exit damage only when it is free
bad: Dying in a 1v4 with the AWP
Forcing every round

prohibitedAdvice: Cheats, scripts, macros, bind exploits, map exploits or anything against Valve’s rules
Ghosting: information from streams, spectators or anything the player cannot see
Leaving a match early or griefing teammates

playbook.title: Crosshair at head level, on the next angle
playbook.principle: Keep your crosshair at head height and on the exact spot an enemy is most likely to appear next, so the fight needs little or no flick. Adjust the height for stairs, boxes and ramps, and move it to the next angle as soon as one is clear.
playbook.why: Leetify measures crosshair placement as the degrees your crosshair moved from first seeing an enemy to first damaging them, and time to damage as the time between those two moments. Rank averages shown on Leetify profiles sit near 12 degrees and about 700 ms at low ranks and nearer 8 degrees and about 550 ms at Premier level (per-profile figures, not a published table). In the Oct 2026 game data an AK-47 head hit does 144 before armour and still kills through a helmet, so a crosshair already on the head wins most rifle duels.
good: Crosshair parked at head height on the edge of the next corner
Raising the crosshair before walking up stairs or a ramp
Moving the crosshair to the next angle once one is clear
bad: Crosshair pointed at the floor or the wall in front of you while moving
Watching the middle of a long lane instead of its edge
Needing a big flick for every enemy
signals: Your view before the fight: the crosshair sits below head height or on a wall when the enemy appears
Death panel: you dealt 0 damage to the player who killed you
Your view: the crosshair travels a long way to the enemy before the first shot
playbook.fix: Park your crosshair at head height on the edge of the next angle before you move into it.
playbook.drill: Yprac Hub prefire mode on each map in the pool: walk every route as T and CT, holding head level on each corner. Then 10 minutes of aim_botz with headshot-only bots, resting the crosshair at head height between targets.

playbook.title: Counter-strafe before you shoot
playbook.principle: Stop before you fire. Tap the opposite movement key (A after D, D after A) to kill your momentum, then shoot. A rifle bullet fired while moving goes wide even when the crosshair is on the head.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 game data: the AK-47 standing inaccuracy is 0.0064 against 0.175 at full running speed, about 27 times worse; the scoped AWP is about 88 times worse moving than standing. Community testing puts the accurate threshold near 34 percent of the weapon top speed (about 73 units per second for the AK-47, whose top speed is 215), so you need to be almost stopped. Leetify tracks proper counter-strafing as the share of shots fired after a good stop; rank averages shown on profiles sit around 75 to 83 percent (unverified as a table).
good: Short strafe, stop, shoot, strafe back
Shooting only once your movement has stopped
Using the opposite key instead of just letting go of the key
bad: Shooting while running to the next cover
Holding W while spraying
Jumping or running shots with a rifle
signals: Your view: the screen is still sliding sideways when you fire
Bullet marks land well away from the crosshair on the wall behind the enemy
Death panel: several shots fired at close range but 0 damage given
playbook.fix: Tap the opposite strafe key to stop dead, then fire your first bullet.
playbook.drill: aim_botz or a private server: strafe left and right between two bots and only shoot after a counter-strafe; turn on the speed readout (cl_showpos 1) to see when you are near 0. Track the Leetify counter-strafing stat week to week.

playbook.title: Make the first bullet count
playbook.principle: The first bullet of a rifle is its most accurate. Stand still, aim at the head and fire one clean shot before you think about spraying. At range, tap and let the gun settle between shots instead of holding the trigger.
playbook.why: Each shot adds inaccuracy that decays over the weapon recovery time: about 0.37 s for the AK-47 and 0.34 s for the M4A4 when standing (Oct 2026 game data). Tapping faster than that stacks inaccuracy. Derived from the same data: the AK-47 kills a helmeted player with one head hit at normal ranges (36 damage x4, 77.5 percent armour penetration), while both M4 rifles do about 92 to a helmeted head, so CTs need a second hit.
good: One aimed shot at the head, then a short burst if needed
Pausing about a third of a second between taps at long range
Expecting to need two head hits with an M4 against a helmet
bad: Opening a long-range fight with a full spray
Clicking as fast as possible at range
Spraying at a target 40 metres away
signals: Your view: tracers fan out above the enemy head at range
Death panel: a few hits given but low damage in a long-range duel
Scoreboard HS% falling while your kills stay low
playbook.fix: Fire one aimed shot at head height and let the crosshair settle before the next one.
playbook.drill: aim_botz long-range setting: 50 kills with single taps only, then 50 with two-shot bursts; practise the tap rhythm on a wall at 20 metres.

playbook.title: Spray, burst or tap by range
playbook.principle: Choose how you shoot by distance. Up close, spray and pull down. At mid range, fire short bursts and reset. At long range, tap single shots. If the first bullets miss at range, step back into cover instead of spraying.
playbook.why: Guides agree the AK-47 pattern climbs sharply over the first bullets and spread takes over late in the spray (around bullet 15 per one guide). Range also lowers damage: the AK-47 keeps 98 percent of its damage per 500 units while the MAC-10 keeps 80 percent and the UMP-45 75 percent (Oct 2026 range modifiers), so SMGs lose long fights.
good: Full spray with pull-down inside about 10 metres
Bursts of two to five bullets at mid range
Single taps across long lanes
bad: Holding the trigger at 30 metres
Taking long fights with an SMG or shotgun
Spraying, missing and staying in the open
signals: Your view: the crosshair stays still while tracers climb above the target
Kill feed: you die to a rifle at long range while holding an SMG
HUD ammo counter empty at the moment you die
playbook.fix: Match the trigger to the distance: spray only up close, burst at mid range and tap at long range.
playbook.drill: Recoil Master workshop map for the AK-47 and M4 patterns (first 10 bullets), then aim_botz bursts at three set distances.

playbook.title: Clear one angle at a time
playbook.principle: When you enter an area, slice it: take each angle one by one from cover, pre-aiming the common spots, so only one enemy can see you at a time. Prefire spots where a player is very likely to be.
playbook.why: Fighting two angles at once means you can only aim at one of them. Prefire routes on practice maps teach the common holding spots on each map, and Leetify time to damage improves when the crosshair is already on those spots.
good: Peeking one corner while the rest stay blocked by the wall
Pre-aiming the common spot as you swing
Asking a teammate to cover the angle you cannot
bad: Walking into the middle of a site where four angles can see you
Turning your back on an unchecked corner
Leaving the closest corners until last
signals: Radar: you stand in the open centre of a site with enemies around it
Kill feed: you die to a player from an angle you had not looked at
Your view: the killer appears at the side of the screen, not near the crosshair
playbook.fix: Clear the closest angle first and keep the others blocked behind cover until you are ready for them.
playbook.drill: Yprac Hub prefire routes for each map in the pool, both sides; walk them slowly with counter-strafes, then at full pace.

playbook.title: Reload behind cover, not in the fight
playbook.principle: Since March 2026 a reload throws away the bullets left in the magazine, so only reload when you are safe and the magazine is low. If a fight starts with a nearly empty magazine, switch to your pistol rather than reloading in front of an enemy.
playbook.why: Valve reworked reloading in March 2026: the current magazine and its remaining rounds are dropped and a fresh one comes from reserve, now counted in magazines (Oct 2026 game data: AK-47 30 plus 3 spare magazines, M4A4 30 plus 4, M4A1-S 20 plus 3, AWP 5 plus 2). Attacks are blocked for about 2.5 s (AK-47) to 3.1 s (M4) after a reload starts. The September 2026 Rush Hour update added a slower silent reload by holding the reload key.
good: Reloading after a kill only once you are back behind cover
Switching to the pistol to finish a fight
Counting bullets during a spray
bad: Reloading after every two shots and throwing away rounds
Reloading in the open next to the player you just killed
Running dry on the last enemy
signals: HUD ammo counter at 0 or the reload animation playing when you die
Your death comes within 3 seconds of starting a reload
HUD reserve magazines run out before the end of a long round
playbook.fix: Reload only from cover and switch to your pistol when the magazine runs dry mid-fight.
playbook.drill: Deathmatch with one rule: no reload in the open, and switch to the pistol under 5 bullets.

playbook.title: Jiggle peek for information
playbook.principle: When you only need to know whether an angle is held, jiggle: a quick strafe out and back that shows a little of you for a moment. Use it to bait a shot or spot a player, then decide with the team. Do not jiggle and then wide swing the same angle straight away.
playbook.why: MetaBot puts it simply: a jiggle asks a question, a wide peek commits to an answer. Against an AWP, a jiggle that draws the shot opens the bolt cycle of 1.455 s (Oct 2026 game data).
good: One short jiggle, then calling what you saw
Jiggling to bait the AWP shot before a teammate swings
Jiggling from a spot with cover on both sides
bad: Jiggling slowly and showing your whole body
Jiggling the same angle again and again until you are pre-aimed
Shooting while jiggling
signals: Kill feed: you die to an AWP or rifle at an angle you had already shown
Your view: several peeks of the same corner in a row before the death
Death panel: 0 damage given
playbook.fix: Jiggle once, call what you saw, and change the angle or wait for a teammate before you peek again.
playbook.drill: Private server with a friend: one holds with an AWP, the other jiggles from cover; count how often the holder gets a clean shot.

playbook.title: Wide swing with a plan
playbook.principle: Wide swing when you want to take a fight against a player holding a close angle, ideally behind a flash or with a teammate ready to trade. Swing far enough to see the whole angle at once, stop and shoot. As a defender, avoid wide swinging into attackers who are waiting for it.
playbook.why: A wide swing uses peeker's advantage: the player moving into the fight tends to see the holder slightly earlier. Guides say it still exists in CS2, though smaller than in CS:GO. A wide swing that loses the duel leaves you in the open with no way back, so it needs a flash or a trader.
good: Wide swing behind a teammate's pop flash
Swinging with a teammate one second behind you to trade
Counter-strafing at the end of the swing before shooting
bad: Wide swinging alone into two enemies
Swinging and shooting while still moving
Swinging as a CT into the attackers' crossfire
signals: Radar: you are the only player on your team in that area when you swing
Kill feed: you die first and nobody trades within 5 seconds
Your view: the screen is still moving when you fire
playbook.fix: Wide swing only with a flash or a trader ready, and stop moving before you shoot.
playbook.drill: Prefire routes taking wide swings; in a private server with a friend, practise the flash-then-swing timing until the swing starts as the flash pops.

playbook.title: Shoulder peek the AWP, then punish
playbook.principle: Against an AWP, do not dry peek. Show just your shoulder to bait the shot, then use the bolt time to swing with a rifle or let a teammate swing. If the AWP does not shoot, smoke or flash it instead.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 game data: the AWP needs 1.455 s between shots and moves at 100 units per second when scoped. It does 115 damage with 97.5 percent armour penetration, so any upper body hit kills, but a leg hit does not. A shoulder peek risks little and wins the timing.

playbook.fix: Bait the AWP with a shoulder peek or blind it with utility before you cross its lane.
playbook.drill: With a friend: one holds a lane with the AWP, the other practises shoulder peeks and swings in the bolt window; count the successful swings.

playbook.title: Use or deny peeker's advantage
playbook.principle: The player who moves into the fight usually sees the other a moment earlier. On attack, use it with quick, committed peeks. On defence, deny it: hold from further back or from an off-angle, so the peeker has to search for you, and let them come to you.
playbook.why: GGRecon and CSDB describe peeker's advantage as still present in CS2, though smaller than in CS:GO. Holding a few metres back from a corner gives the holder more of the peeker's movement to react to, and moving after each contact breaks the peeker's timing.

Swinging fast and stopping, instead of slowly walking out
Changing position after each contact

playbook.fix: Hold angles from a few metres back or off the common spot, and peek fast and committed when you are the one moving.

playbook.title: Hold angles and off-angles as a defender
playbook.principle: As a CT, let the attackers come to you. Hold one angle at a time from a spot they do not pre-aim, with cover to fall back to. Do not wide swing into attackers who have flashes and traders; fall back and wait for help or utility instead.
playbook.why: Off-angles force the attacker to re-aim and cost them time (bo3.gg, CSDB). The CT side wins on time: every second an attacker spends clearing comes off the 1:55 round (Oct 2026 competitive config).

playbook.title: Do not re-peek the same angle
playbook.principle: After a kill, a miss or being spotted, the enemy knows where you are. Move, change height or wait before showing again. Re-peeking the same angle meets a pre-aimed enemy.
playbook.why: AWP and holding guides agree: once your position is revealed, enemies pre-fire that exact spot (Refrag). Changing position even slightly can break a peeker's timing (CSDB). The safest re-peek is behind a flash, ideally thrown by a teammate.

playbook.title: Do not die in the open
playbook.principle: Cross open ground only when a smoke, a flash or a teammate covers it, and cross at full speed. Stop behind cover, not in the middle of a lane, and avoid places where several enemies can see you at once.
playbook.why: You cannot counter-strafe and shoot back while crossing, so a player already holding the lane gets a free shot. Open spots also expose you to more than one angle, and a duel against two angles is usually lost.

playbook.fix: Cross open ground only behind a smoke or flash and stop where cover protects you.

playbook.title: Play around enemy utility
playbook.principle: Read enemy utility. Turn away from flashes, leave fire instead of standing in it, do not hold the edge of a smoke where you can be pushed, and expect a push just after fresh utility lands.
playbook.why: Per CSDB, fire deals about 40 HP per second and lasts about 7 s for a molotov and about 5.5 s for an incendiary (the incendiary was cut in May 2024). An HE does up to about 98 to an unarmoured player and 57 to an armoured one. A blind player rarely wins a duel, and the kill feed marks a flash assist with a flashbang icon beside the assister.

playbook.fix: Turn away from flashes, step out of fire and retake your angle from a new spot once the utility ends.

playbook.title: Trade your teammates
playbook.principle: Move with a teammate close enough that, if they die, you can kill their killer within a few seconds. Do not stack on top of each other, and do not lag so far behind that the enemy can reset. If you go in first, play for the trade.
playbook.why: KAST counts a round as useful if you were traded; stat tools commonly use a 5-second trade window (awpy default; HLTV does not publish its exact window). SCOPE.GG data from 2026 Premier and FACEIT matches show the team with the opening kill wins about 65 to 73 percent of rounds, so trading the opening death quickly wins back the numbers.

playbook.fix: Stay a short swing behind your teammate and peek their killer the moment they die.

playbook.title: Short, useful calls
playbook.principle: Call what you see in a few words: how many, where, what weapon and their health if you hit them. Then go quiet. When you die, give one clear call and stop talking.
playbook.why: Comms guides agree: avoid the vague they, count and name what you see, stack callout plus number plus weapon, and go silent after the information. Dead players who report clearly help the living ones win rounds.

playbook.title: Entry with support
playbook.principle: As the entry, your job is to take the first fight and make space, not to survive at any cost. Enter behind a flash, take the most dangerous close angle first and keep moving so a teammate can trade you.
playbook.why: Entries die often; a traded entry still counts towards KAST and keeps the numbers even. Refrag lists poor spacing and timing among the worst entry mistakes.

playbook.title: IGL basics: simple calls, clear plan
playbook.principle: An in-game leader sets a plan before the round, reads what happens and makes one clear mid-round call. Keep it simple: a default, a target site, the buy and a backup. Give everyone a role so they know their job.
playbook.why: Role guides describe the IGL as the player who calls the buy and the strategy; most uncoordinated rounds fail on mixed buys and late, unclear calls rather than on aim.

playbook.title: Lurk with purpose

playbook.why: BLAST's lurker guide: a lurker threatens a second area, slows CT rotations and catches players moving between sites. A lurker who dies early leaves the team a player down with nothing gained.

playbook.title: Smoke to cut sightlines

playbook.why: Smokes last roughly 18 to 20 s in CS2 (guides differ). Since July 2026 a bomb explosion clears nearby smoke for a few seconds. Bullets pass through smoke, and the kill feed marks a through-smoke kill with a smoke icon.

playbook.why: Refrag's teamplay fundamentals: a crossfire forces the attacker to deal with two angles at once, and it turns a lost first duel into a trade instead of a lost site.

playbook.why: BLAST's anchor guide describes the anchor's main job as holding the site until help comes. Since September 2026 reloads (held key) and unscoping can be silent, which pros such as donk and sh1ro called good for anchors and clutch players.

playbook.title: Split hits
playbook.principle: A split attacks one site from two directions at once, so the defenders must face two ways. Both groups need to arrive together; if one is early, the defenders fight them one group at a time.
playbook.why: bo3.gg on split pushes: timing decides whether a split works, and an early group lets the defenders fight one side before the second arrives.
good: Both groups calling their timing
Starting the hit when both are in position
Using the split to catch rotating CTs
bad: One group entering alone
Splitting without enough players for each side
Losing the timing on a long walk
signals: Kill feed: deaths from one group, then from the other group 10 or more seconds later
Radar: one group on site while the other is still far away
Round lost with more than two attackers still alive
playbook.fix: Hit only when both groups are in position and call the moment you go.

playbook.title: Fakes that sell
playbook.principle: A fake shows pressure on one site to pull defenders, then the team hits the other. It needs noise and utility that look real, and it needs players already close to the real target. Keep it cheap: a few grenades and some sound, not five players.
playbook.why: bo3.gg: pro teams rarely send all five into a fake, and a fake without map control is easy for defenders to read.
good: Two players making noise and throwing utility
The rest of the team waiting near the real site
Hitting the real site as the CTs rotate
bad: Faking with the whole team and running across the map
Faking with no utility
Hitting the real site too late after the fake
signals: Round timer: the real hit starts with under 25 seconds left after a fake
Radar: all five Ts on the fake site
Kill feed: Ts die on the way from the fake to the real site
playbook.fix: Fake with two players and utility while the rest wait close to the real site.

playbook.title: Use the clock on attack
playbook.principle: Know the clock. A competitive round lasts 1:55. Use the early time to gather information, and start the final hit with enough time to plant and hold. A hit that starts with only a few seconds left often fails before the plant.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 competitive config: round time 1.92 minutes (1:55), freeze time 15 s, buy time 20 s. The bomb timer is 40 s, and a defuse takes 10 s, or 5 s with a kit (CSDB, GGRecon). If time runs out, the round ends with the message Bombing failed.
good: Checking the timer before each call
Planting with time left for a post-plant
Speeding up as the clock runs low
bad: Running out of time without planting
Walking slowly onto a site at 0:15
Rushing out of spawn with no plan every round
signals: Round end banner: Bombing failed (CTs won on time)
Round timer under 0:20 with the bomb not planted
Radar: the bomb carrier far from both sites late in the round
playbook.fix: Check the timer at every call and start the final hit with enough time to plant and hold.

playbook.title: Mid-round: play the numbers
playbook.principle: After the first kills, think again. With more players alive, slow down, group up and trade; do not hand back the advantage with lone peeks. With fewer, use utility and the clock, or save if the round is gone. Ask where the enemy is weak right now.
playbook.why: SCOPE.GG 2026 data: the team with the opening kill wins about 65 to 73 percent of rounds, and the advantage grows when the team keeps trading. Leetify Rating credits changes in round win chance, so throwing away a numbers advantage costs a lot.
good: After an opening kill, the team groups and hits the weaker site
Saying we are up, no solo peeks
Down 3v5, deciding early whether to save

Chasing kills after the plan has worked
Forcing a 2v4 retake with no utility
signals: Kill feed: your death while your team had more players alive

Round lost after being 5v3 up
playbook.fix: When your team is ahead on numbers, group up and trade instead of taking solo fights.

playbook.title: Post-plant: crossfire and play the time
playbook.principle: After the plant, the CTs must come to you. Spread into positions that watch the bomb from different angles, away from each other, and let the clock work. Do not peek the CTs; wait for the defuse or the retake and shoot then. Keep utility to stop the defuse.
playbook.why: Refrag's afterplant tips: a bad plant spot can ruin a good hold. Bomb timer 40 s; a defuse takes 10 s without a kit and 5 s with one (CSDB, GGRecon). Since July 2026 the explosion clears smoke and puts out fire in its radius, and a T team that plants but loses gets $600 extra (Oct 2026 config).
good: Holding the bomb from two different angles
A molotov or smoke on the bomb when a CT starts to defuse
Waiting for the CTs to make the first move
bad: Peeking out to hunt CTs with 30 seconds on the bomb
All Ts standing on top of the bomb
Throwing all utility before the CTs arrive
signals: Kill feed: you die to a CT after leaving your post-plant spot
Round timer: bomb planted and you die with more than 20 seconds left on it
Round end banner: Bomb defused
playbook.fix: Hold a post-plant angle on the bomb, wait for the defuse and throw your molotov or HE when it starts.

playbook.title: Retake together
playbook.principle: When the site falls, wait for teammates, then retake as a group with utility. Clear the post-plant positions one at a time, trade each other and only defuse when it is safe or the clock forces you.
playbook.why: Refrag's retake tips: avoid taking first contact alone. With a kit you need 5 s to defuse and 10 s without it, against a 40 s bomb timer, so a grouped retake usually has time. Valve added an official Retakes mode in October 2025 for practice.

playbook.fix: Group up with your teammates and utility, then retake together and clear before you defuse.

playbook.title: Defuse safely
playbook.principle: Only stick the defuse when the remaining Ts are dead, blind or blocked. Smoke the bomb so you cannot be seen while defusing, and have a teammate cover you. If you need to bait, tap the defuse and hold the angle; stick it when the clock forces you.
playbook.why: A defuse takes 10 s without a kit and 5 s with a $400 kit (Oct 2026 data). Guides recommend tapping instead of sticking in smoke when an enemy may swing late, and note that each fake restarts the defuse bar.

playbook.fix: Smoke the bomb and have a teammate cover you before you stick the defuse.

playbook.title: Do not die to the bomb
playbook.principle: When you cannot finish the defuse in time, leave the blast and save. Know where the bomb is and how far its damage reaches; since July 2026 your health bar flashes red to show the expected bomb damage once the bomb can be heard.
playbook.why: The July 8 2026 update redesigned the explosion with damage baked into each map, and the July 20/21 update shows the damage preview once the bomb is audible (Insider Gaming, Dust2.us). A bomb death loses the weapon as well as the round.

playbook.fix: Get out of the blast when you cannot finish the defuse and keep your weapon for the next round.

playbook.title: Clutch: one fight at a time
playbook.principle: In a 1vX, take one duel at a time: use sound and the radar to find an isolated enemy, fight from angles where only one can see you and use the clock. As a T with the bomb planted, let them come; as a CT, the bomb timer pushes you, so pick your moment early.
playbook.why: ProSettings: 1v1s are winnable while 1v2 and 1v3 usually need you to isolate. One analysis of over 200,000 pro matches (2021) put 1v2 wins near 19 percent, 1v3 near 4 percent and 1v4 near 0.6 percent (unverified).

Fighting from a spot that only one enemy can see at a time
Tapping the defuse to bait a peek

signals: Team counter at the top of the HUD: you are last alive against two or more

Your movement: running at full speed in the final 30 seconds
playbook.fix: Isolate one enemy at a time, stay quiet and let the clock work for you.
playbook.drill: Refrag clutch mode or retake servers: play 1v2 and 1v3 situations and review each loss for the moment two enemies saw you at once.

playbook.title: Last alive: save or play
playbook.principle: When you are last alive, decide quickly whether the round can be won. If the time, the numbers or the bomb make it lost, save your weapon for the next round. If it can be won, play one isolated fight at a time.
playbook.why: Keeping an AK-47 ($2,700), an M4 ($2,900) or the AWP ($4,750) saves that money for the next buy (Oct 2026 prices). A 1v4 is rarely won (about 0.6 percent in pro play by one analysis, unverified).

Hiding far from the bomb after the plant
Playing the clutch only with time, position and information

Saving with a minute left in a 1v1
Running onto the site with 5 seconds on the bomb

playbook.fix: When the round is lost, hide and keep your weapon instead of taking a 1v4.

playbook.title: Buy together
playbook.principle: Buy as a team. A full buy is a rifle, armour, a kit for CTs and grenades for every player. If not everyone can full buy, the team saves together, forces together, or half-buys only if everyone can still full buy next round.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 prices: a T full buy (AK-47, Kevlar and Helmet, smoke, two flashes, molotov) costs $4,800; a CT full buy (M4, Kevlar and Helmet, kit, smoke, two flashes, incendiary) costs $5,500. Guides suggest a full eco below about $2,000 each after a loss and a force around $2,500 to $3,500 before a bonus round (sources differ).

playbook.fix: Check the team money on the scoreboard and make the same buy call as your teammates.

playbook.title: Know the loss bonus
playbook.principle: Losing pays a loss bonus that rises with each loss in a row: $1,400, $1,900, $2,400, $2,900, up to $3,400. Each half starts with one loss counted, so losing the pistol round pays $1,900. Plan saves and forces around it.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 competitive config: cash_team_loser_bonus 1400, plus 500 per consecutive loss, mp_starting_losses 1. Round wins pay $3,250 (elimination or time) or $3,500 (bomb detonated or defused), and a T team that plants but loses gets $600 more since May 2024. Most 2026 guides say a win lowers the loss count by one step instead of resetting it, though some still describe a reset (unverified). The scoreboard Loss Bonus tooltip shows what your team will earn with a loss.
good: Reading the Loss Bonus on the scoreboard before the buy
Saving when a loss still gives a full buy next round
Forcing when the enemy is weak and your loss bonus is high
bad: Forcing every round after the pistol loss
Ignoring that a loss now still pays well
Thinking a single win resets your saving plan
signals: Scoreboard Loss Bonus tooltip: low value while the team forces again
Scoreboard money: everyone under $2,000 two rounds in a row
Round end: lost force followed by a broken full buy
playbook.fix: Read the Loss Bonus on the scoreboard and plan the next two rounds of buys with it.

playbook.title: Save when the round is lost
playbook.principle: When the round cannot be won, keep your weapon. Save together, hide away from the bomb and away from where the enemies will look, and stay alive to start the next round with a gun.
playbook.why: A saved rifle is worth $2,700 to $2,900 and the AWP $4,750 (Oct 2026 prices). Guides say the common mistake is uneven saving: one player keeps a rifle while others die with theirs, and the team buys unevenly next round.

playbook.title: Drop weapons for teammates
playbook.principle: If you have money to spare and a teammate cannot buy, buy and drop them a rifle so the whole team plays a full round. Ask for drops in the freeze time, and pick up a dead teammate's weapon when it is safe.
playbook.why: The buy menu has Buy and Throw (hold the key) to buy for a teammate, and the money cap is $16,000, so money above what you need is wasted. Guides treat dropping a rifle as a normal economy move.

playbook.fix: Buy and drop a rifle for any teammate who cannot afford one when you have the spare money.

playbook.title: Anti-eco discipline
playbook.principle: Against an eco, play tight and trade. Do not give away free kills and rifles with lone peeks; hold together, use the range advantage of your weapons and expect a rush. A cheap SMG earns twice the kill reward of a rifle.
playbook.why: Kill rewards in the Oct 2026 data: $300 for rifles and pistols, $600 for most SMGs (the P90 pays $300), $900 for the Nova, MAG-7 and Sawed-Off, $600 for the XM1014, $100 for the AWP, $1,500 for the knife. A lost anti-eco hands the enemy your rifles and resets their economy.

Moving in pairs and trading
Buying an SMG for the extra kill reward
bad: Pushing into close corners alone against pistols
Dropping your rifle to an eco rush
Peeking a stacked eco site with no utility
signals: Scoreboard: enemy team money low and your team loses the round
Kill feed: you die to a pistol while holding a rifle
Next round: enemies holding your team's rifles
playbook.fix: Against an eco, hold range and trade in pairs instead of taking close, lone fights.

playbook.title: Pistol rounds
playbook.principle: The pistol round starts with $800. Agree a plan, buy as a team and fight in groups so you can trade. Kevlar protects the body but not the head, and starting pistols kill with one head hit on a player with no helmet at close range.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 data: Kevlar costs $650 and Kevlar plus Helmet $1,000, so nobody has a helmet on the pistol round. Derived from the same data, a USP-S head hit does about 140 and a Glock-18 head hit about 120 up close, both lethal without a helmet. Losing the pistol round pays $1,900. Common buys are Kevlar alone, or a P250 ($300) or Tec-9 ($500, T only) with a grenade.

Fighting in pairs for trades
Aiming for the head on every shot

Buying utility you never throw
signals: Round 1 or 13 kill feed: your death untraded
Your view: shots aimed at chest height on the pistol round
Scoreboard money after round 1: teammates bought different loadouts
playbook.fix: Play the pistol round with a teammate, aim for the head and buy what the team agreed.

playbook.title: AWP: reposition and do not overpeek
playbook.principle: With the AWP, take one shot from a position, then move. Hold angles instead of wide peeking, have a fallback for the bolt time, and play with a teammate who can trade if you miss. The AWP is your team's most valuable weapon; do not throw it away.
playbook.why: Oct 2026 data: the AWP costs $4,750, earns only $100 per kill, needs 1.455 s between shots and drops to 100 units per second when scoped. Refrag's first AWP tip is a fallback angle after every shot, hit or miss.

Holding a long angle with a teammate covering the close one
Falling back behind cover to re-bolt
bad: Peeking the same angle twice in a row
Wide peeking a rifler at close range
Dying with the AWP early in the round
signals: Kill feed: your AWP kill followed within seconds by your death at the same spot
Kill feed: you die holding the AWP in the first 30 seconds
Your view: you stay scoped in after missing a shot
playbook.fix: Take one shot, then move to your fallback angle before the enemy can answer.
playbook.drill: Refrag AWP Hold mode or a private server with a friend: practise shot, unscope, step behind cover and re-peek a different angle.

playbook.title: Sound discipline
playbook.principle: Running makes footsteps the enemy can hear; walking (Shift) and crouch-walking do not. Walk when you are close to enemies, when you lurk and in clutches. Run when speed matters more than surprise, such as a rotation or an execute.
playbook.why: CSDB: walking is the silent way to move, and switching weapons is silent. Since September 2026 holding the reload key gives a silent but slower reload, and unscoping is silent. Pros said the change helps anchors and clutch players.

bad: Running up to an angle you want to hold quietly

Running in a 1v2
signals: Your movement: full running speed in the last few metres before a surprise peek
Kill feed: you die to a player who was already aimed at your path

playbook.fix: Walk when you are near enemies or in a clutch, and run only when speed is worth the noise.

playbook.title: Review each death: what, where, why
playbook.principle: After each death, read the facts: who killed you, with what, from where, and whether you were traded. Then ask one question: what would have saved me? Fix the pattern that repeats, not the one-off.
playbook.why: The CS2 death panel shows the killer, their remaining health and the weapon (its layout also has damage taken and given rows); the kill feed shows headshot, wallbang, through-smoke, blind-attacker and flash-assist icons; the round-end report shows damage per enemy. Patterns across many deaths tell you more than any single one.

Checking whether your death was traded
Looking for the same mistake across several rounds
bad: Blaming luck every time
Ignoring the kill feed after death
Changing everything after one bad round
signals: Death panel: killer name, weapon and the damage given and taken lines
Kill feed: icons beside your death (headshot, wallbang, smoke, blind, flash assist)
Round-end report: damage given and taken under each enemy portrait
playbook.fix: After each death, name one thing you could change and watch for it in the next rounds.

maps.name: Ancient
maps.setting: Ruined Mesoamerican temple complex in a jungle: mossy stone blocks, carved walls, steps, water channels and dense green plants. The CS2 files also contain a night variant (de_ancient_night) with its own radar.
maps.layout: On the official radar CT Spawn is top centre and T Spawn bottom centre. A site is top-left, very close to CT Spawn; Ts reach it by the long A Main route up the west side or through Donut from Mid. B site is on the right; Ts reach it by Water and B Ramp from T Spawn or via the Mid ledges and Cave. Mid climbs north by stairs to House and the CT side. CTs reach A in about 4-5 s but need about 8-9.5 s for B.

callouts.name: T Spawn
callouts.look: Sunken stone court with steps at the bottom centre of the radar, surrounded by mossy temple walls and jungle plants.
callouts.use: Ts start here. Paths: north-west along the long A Main route, east through Water to B Ramp, and north toward Mid. Valve's 'Top Mid and Donut' smokes are thrown from here.

callouts.name: A Main Stairs
callouts.look: Stone steps on the long, low A Main route west of T Spawn.
callouts.use: Valve-named spot ('a main bottom stairs') on the way to A; a meeting point for A Main pushes and lurks.

callouts.name: A Main Entrance
callouts.look: Turn where the A Main route bends north toward A, next to stone walls.
callouts.use: Valve-named spot ('a main entrance'). Valve's 'Donut' and 'CT' smokes for an A hit are thrown from just south of here.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.look: Long stone corridor running north along the west side of the map toward A, with pillars and side rooms.
callouts.use: Main T route to A. CTs on A and in Donut hold its exit; Ts throw the A execute smokes from its southern end.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.look: Stone plaza top-left with temple walls, steps and blocks for cover; the CT entrance is on its east side and the Donut exit to the south.
callouts.use: Bomb site A. Very close to CT Spawn. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'for A main', 'for donut', 'mid site'.

callouts.name: A CT
callouts.look: Corridor from CT Spawn west into A along the top of the map.
callouts.use: CT entrance to A (about 4-5 s from spawn). Valve's 'CT' smoke from A Main lands here to cut rotations on an A execute.

callouts.name: Donut
callouts.look: Ring-shaped (octagonal) room around a central block between Mid and A.
callouts.use: Connector from Mid to A and a contested spot for both sides. Valve's 'Donut' smoke from A Main covers its A-side exit; another Valve smoke from T Spawn covers its Mid side. Named on the loading screen.

callouts.name: Mid
callouts.look: Central open area with stone ruins and steps, rising north toward CT.
callouts.use: Central control zone linking Donut, the CT stairs and the route toward B.

callouts.name: Bottom Mid
callouts.look: Lower (south) half of Mid near the ledges.
callouts.use: Valve-named spot; Ts gather here to take Mid or to split toward Cave and B.

callouts.name: Top Mid
callouts.look: Upper (north) half of Mid at the foot of the stairs up to the CT side.
callouts.use: Valve-named spot. Ts use Valve's 'Top Mid' smoke from T Spawn (it lands at the top of the stairs) to cross safely.

callouts.name: CT Mid
callouts.look: Stairway climbing from Mid up to the CT side, narrow and walled.
callouts.use: Valve's 'top mid CT'. CTs hold Mid from the top; Ts need the Top Mid smoke to walk up.

callouts.name: House

maps.spawns: CT Spawn top centre, T Spawn bottom centre. Estimated minimum run times (shortest line across the CS2 nav mesh from the spawn-zone centre to the edge of the plant zone; knife 250 u/s to AK 215 u/s; real runs are a little slower, and a nav-area-centre route gave values up to about 30% higher): CT to A about 4-5 s, CT to B about 8-9.5 s; T to A about 15-17.5 s (shortest via Mid and Donut; the A Main route is longer), T to B about 12.5-14.5 s; A to B about 10.5-12 s.

modeTips.t: Default: take Mid with Valve's 'Top Mid and Donut' smokes from T Spawn, keep one player in A Main and one at Water for information. A execute: from the south end of A Main throw Valve's 'CT' smoke (A CT) and 'Donut' smoke, molotov the near corners, flash over the A Main exit and hit with a Donut player joining. B execute: from the bottom of B Ramp throw Valve's 'Left and Right Side' smokes (CT entrances), molotov the pillar sides, flash over Ramp Top and push with a Cave split from Mid.
modeTips.ct: Common 2-1-2: two A (site and Donut), one Mid (House/CT Mid, often the AWP), two B (Ramp Top or site, plus Cave or B CT). A is close to CT Spawn (about 4-5 s), so A can be played with fewer players and fast retakes; B is far, so B players should hold for time with molotovs on the ramp and Valve's CT 'Ramp' smoke.
modeTips.pistol: T: fast B Ramp with flashes or a Mid-to-Donut A hit. CT: stack B with three since A is quick to retake; keep flashes for the retake.
modeTips.retake: A: come from A CT and Donut together, smoke the A Main exit, flash over and clear the corners. B: Valve 'Ramp' smoke from the CT side, enter from B CT and Cave together, clear both sides of the pillar.
modeTips.postplant: A plant: hold from A Main and Donut and expect a fast CT arrival; save a molotov for the default plant. B plant: hold from the ramp, Cave and one spot watching B CT; molotov the default plant from Ramp Top.

maps.weaponFit: AWP: CT Mid/House down Mid, Ramp Top on B, A site toward A Main; T AWP from Bottom Mid or the bottom of B Ramp. Rifles: Mid control, site holds. SMGs and shotguns: Donut, Cave and close corners around both sites; strong on CT force buys. Molotovs at Ramp Top and Donut buy the most time.
mistakes: Walking into Mid without the Top Mid smoke
Hitting A without smoking the A CT entrance, which CTs reach in seconds
Pushing up B Ramp with no Cave pressure or side smokes
CT B players giving up the ramp without using molotovs first
Leaving Donut uncontested so Ts split A through it
Late B rotation: CTs need about 8-9.5 s from spawn and longer from A
Forgetting to clear both sides of the B pillar after planting

searchAndDestroy.A notes: Top-left plaza next to CT Spawn. Ts arrive from A Main (west) and Donut (south); CTs from A CT within seconds. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'for A main', 'for donut', 'mid site'. Retake: CTs come straight from spawn through A CT and from Mid through Donut; smoke the A Main exit and flash over the site.
searchAndDestroy.B notes: Plaza on the right with a central pillar. Ts arrive up B Ramp from Water and through Cave from Mid; CTs from B CT and the north-east side. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'for back CT', 'for ramp', 'for CT'. Retake: smoke Ramp Top (Valve CT 'Ramp' lineup) to cut T support, enter from B CT and Cave together and clear the pillar sides.

utilityPlans.name: A take from A Main
utilityPlans.how: From outside A Main, throw the CT, Donut and Temple smokes together. Burn the default boxes, then pop the flash and walk out of Main as one group.

utilityPlans.name: B take up the ramp
utilityPlans.how: From Ruins, throw the left and right side smokes and the CT Alley smoke first. Burn Wood and Pillar, then pop the Pillar flash and run up the ramp together.

utilityPlans.name: Mid control
utilityPlans.how: Smoke Top Mid and Donut from spawn, then flash Mid as the first player walks in. Re-smoke Top Mid from Elbow late in the round, and flash Jaguar to split towards B through Cave.

utilityPlans.name: Retake A
utilityPlans.how: Smoke Donut and A Main from CT Spawn so the site becomes one fight. Retake together from CT and trade the first contact.

utilityPlans.name: Retake B
utilityPlans.how: From Back Alley, smoke B Ramp and Cave to cut the site off. Burn the default plant to flush hidden Ts, then walk in together.

maps.name: Anubis
maps.setting: Egyptian riverside town: sandstone buildings and columns, hieroglyph walls, turquoise canals and palms. Revamped and returned to Active Duty on 22 Jan 2026 (Premier Season 4), replacing Train; the revamp moved A site crates up to a walkway and changed Mid and B, so some older callouts and angles may differ.
maps.layout: On the official radar CT Spawn is near the top centre-left and T Spawn at the bottom. A site is top-right, reached by Ts through A Main (east lane) or A Water (channel from the canal); CTs reach A via CT Water/Heaven or Camera. B site is on the left, reached by Ts through B Main (west) or Mid to B; CTs come down past Wood. Mid crosses the canal by a bridge, with Window overlooking it.

callouts.name: T Spawn
callouts.look: Wide sandstone courtyard at the bottom of the radar with Egyptian columns, palms and carved walls.
callouts.use: Ts start here. Paths: north-west up B Main, north into Top Mid, east to T Stairs for A. Valve's 'Window' smoke is thrown from its east side.

callouts.name: T Stairs
callouts.look: Stone stairs east of Mid where the T route meets the canal and the A Water channel.
callouts.use: Junction for T pushes to A. Valve has a CT 'T Stairs' smoke from CT Spawn that lands near the top of the stairs.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.look: Long sandstone lane on the right (east) side running north from T Stairs to the south-east corner of A.
callouts.use: Main T route to A. Plants 'for A main' are named in Valve's retake file; CTs hold its exit from Heaven, Tarp and the site.

callouts.name: A Water
callouts.look: Turquoise water channel running north from the canal toward A, between Mid and A Main.
callouts.use: Second T route to A (Valve calls the spot 'a water'). Valve's T 'Heaven' smoke is thrown from here. CTs hold it from Camera and A.

callouts.name: Tarp
callouts.look: Spot at the south edge of A near a tarp-covered structure, where A Main and A Water arrive.
callouts.use: Valve-named spot ('tarp'); CT hold near the T entrances and a T post-plant spot.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.look: Rounded stone plaza top-right with a raised Heaven platform on its west side and a half wall; site crates were moved up to a walkway in the January 2026 revamp.
callouts.use: Bomb site A. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'advantageous, for A main', 'under heaven', 'under half wall'.

callouts.name: Heaven
callouts.look: Raised platform on the north-west side of A, reached from the CT side and by climbing from site.
callouts.use: Strong CT hold over A Main, A Water and the plant; Valve's T 'Heaven' smoke from A Water blocks it. Valve also names a 'heaven towards CT' path to CT Spawn.

callouts.name: CT Water
callouts.look: Water and path behind (north of) CT Spawn leading east toward A Heaven.
callouts.use: CT rotation route from CT Spawn to A (Valve names a spawn here 'ct spawn water').

callouts.name: CT Spawn
callouts.look: Sandstone court near the top centre-left of the radar.
callouts.use: CTs start here, about 6-7 s from B and 9-10.5 s from A (nav-mesh estimate). Valve's CT smokes for Mid and T Stairs are thrown from here.

callouts.name: Camera
callouts.look: Corridor linking CT Mid to the south-west side of A.
callouts.use: CT rotation link between Mid and A; Valve names spots 'camera' and 'camera towards A'. Watches A Water from the CT side.

callouts.name: CT Mid
callouts.look: CT end of Mid between Camera and the north side of the bridge.
callouts.use: CT control spot for Mid and the hub to A via Camera; Valve-named ('ct mid').

callouts.name: Mid
callouts.look: Open sandstone area in the centre north of the bridge, with stairs and pillars.
callouts.use: Central zone linking CT Mid, the bridge, Window and the B side.

callouts.name: Window
callouts.look: Window/opening on the east side of Mid that looks down toward the bridge and canal.
callouts.use: CT position over Mid named on the loading screen. Valve ships a T smoke and a T molotov for it, thrown from the T side.

callouts.name: Bridge
callouts.look: Stone bridge crossing the canal in the middle of the map.
callouts.use: Main T entry into Mid; Valve's CT 'Mid' smoke from CT Spawn lands here. Valve also names a 'bridge window' spot.

callouts.name: Canal
callouts.look: Turquoise water channel running east-west under the bridge, below Mid level.
callouts.use: Low route linking the bridge area to T Stairs and A Water (Valve: 'under bridge, water'). Water is loud, so movement here gives sound cues.

callouts.name: Top Mid
callouts.look: Open sandstone area on the T side south of the bridge.
callouts.use: T staging spot for Mid and the start of the Mid to B route.

callouts.name: Mid to B
callouts.look: Passage from the T side of Mid north-west toward the B site.
callouts.use: Valve-named route ('mid to b'); Ts use it to split B with B Main.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.look: Long sandstone path from T Spawn north-west up to the south-west side of B.
callouts.use: Main T route to B. Valve's T 'Left B Site' smoke is thrown from its start; plants 'for B main' are named in Valve's retake file.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.look: Square plaza on the left with a central block, an electrical box, a pillar and stone walls.
callouts.use: Bomb site B. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'advantageous, for B main', 'for CT', 'for ebox'.

callouts.name: Pizza
callouts.look: Corner on the far west side of B.
callouts.use: Valve-named spot ('pizza'); CT hold and T post-plant spot on the west side of site.

callouts.name: Pillar
callouts.look: Stone pillar at the south side of B near the B Main entrance.
callouts.use: Cover for CTs holding B Main and for Ts entering; Valve-named ('pillar').

callouts.name: E-box
callouts.look: Electrical box on the south-east side of B, toward the Mid to B approach.
callouts.use: Close CT hold and plant reference ('for ebox' in Valve's retake file).

callouts.name: Cubby
callouts.look: Small recess on the east side of B toward Mid.
callouts.use: CT off-angle and T post-plant hide; Valve-named ('cubby').

callouts.name: Wood
callouts.look: Wooden structure on the north-east side of B on the CT approach from spawn.
callouts.use: CT entrance and hold for B; Valve-named ('wood', 'near wood').

maps.spawns: CT Spawn near the top centre-left; T Spawn at the bottom centre. Estimated minimum run times (shortest line across the CS2 nav mesh from the spawn-zone centre to the edge of the plant zone; knife 250 u/s to AK 215 u/s; real runs are a little slower, and a nav-area-centre route gave values up to about 30% higher): CT to A about 9-10.5 s, CT to B about 6-7 s; T to A about 17-20 s, T to B about 11.5-13 s; A to B about 11-12.5 s. Computed on the current (post-revamp) nav mesh.

modeTips.t: Default: contest Mid at the bridge with Valve's 'Window' smoke and molotov, keep one player at T Stairs/A Water and one in B Main. A execute: Valve 'Heaven' smoke from A Water, smoke Camera if you can, molotov Tarp or the half wall, flash and hit from A Main and A Water together. B execute: Valve 'Left B Site' smoke from the start of B Main, smoke Wood/CT side, molotov E-box or Pillar, flash over the entrance and split with Mid to B.
modeTips.ct: Common 2-1-2: two A (Heaven plus site or Camera), one Mid (Window or CT Mid, often the AWP, rotating either way), two B (one at Pillar/E-box facing the entrances, one at Wood). CT Spawn is closer to B (about 6-7 s) than to A (about 9-10.5 s), so the A players must call early. Valve's CT smokes for Mid and T Stairs from CT Spawn slow pushes.
modeTips.pistol: T: fast B Main with flashes or an A Water plus A Main split. CT: stack the side you expect with three, keep the Mid player alive; listen for water movement on the canal and A Water.
modeTips.retake: A: from Heaven and Camera together, smoke the A Main and A Water exits, flash over, clear Tarp and the half wall. B: through Wood with a flash, and from Mid via Mid to B if possible; clear Pizza, Pillar, E-box and Cubby.
modeTips.postplant: A plant: hold A Main and A Water from outside the site, one player watching Camera; keep a molotov for the default plant. B plant: hold B Main and Mid to B, one player watching Wood; molotov the default plant from the entrance.

maps.weaponFit: AWP: Window or CT Mid for the bridge, Heaven over A, B site toward B Main; T AWP at Top Mid toward the bridge. Rifles: Mid control and site holds. SMGs and shotguns: close B spots (Pizza, Cubby, E-box, Pillar) and Camera; strong on CT force buys. Smokes and molotovs on Window and the channels are worth buying every gun round.
mistakes: Crossing the bridge without smoking Window
Walking through the canal or A Water noisily when trying to be quiet
Hitting A only from A Main and letting Heaven hold one entrance
Late A rotation from CT Spawn (about 9-10.5 s)
Not clearing Pizza, Cubby and E-box on B
Relying on pre-2026 angles: the January 2026 revamp changed A, Mid and B
Losing Mid for free so Ts split B through Mid to B

searchAndDestroy.A notes: Rounded plaza top-right with Heaven on its west side and a half wall. Ts arrive from A Main and A Water (both meet near Tarp); CTs from Heaven/CT Water and Camera. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'advantageous, for A main', 'under heaven', 'under half wall'. Retake: Heaven and Camera at the same time, smoke A Main or A Water to cut T support, clear Tarp and the half wall.
searchAndDestroy.B notes: Square plaza on the left with Pizza (west), Pillar (south), E-box (south-east), Cubby (east) and Wood (north-east). Ts arrive from B Main and Mid to B; CTs from Wood. Plants named in Valve's retake file: default, 'advantageous, for B main', 'for CT', 'for ebox'. Retake: come through Wood with a flash and from Mid if Mid is yours; clear Pizza, Pillar, E-box and Cubby.

utilityPlans.name: A execute through Water
utilityPlans.how: Smoke Heaven from Water and Camera from the rugs. Burn the front of A, then pop the A site flash as the group leaves the water together.

utilityPlans.name: B execute through B Main
utilityPlans.how: Throw Left B Site from spawn on the way, then the B CT smoke from B Main. Damage and burn Pillar, pop the entry flash and run in together.

utilityPlans.name: Mid take
utilityPlans.how: Smoke Top Mid and Window from spawn, then burn the new Mid hole. Ts then hold Bridge and can split to A Water or B.

utilityPlans.name: Retake A

maps.name: Cache
maps.setting: Industrial depot near Pripyat/Chernobyl: concrete yards, warehouses, shipping containers, trucks, forklifts and hazard barrels. The CS2 map is a Source 2 rebuild of FMPONE's Cache (Valve bought the rights in May 2025), released 28-29 Apr 2026 with a much brighter, cleaner look than CS:GO's 'green Cache'. Joined Active Duty in Premier Season 5 (July 2026), replacing Overpass.
maps.layout: On the official radar CT Spawn is far left (west) and T Spawn far right (east); both sites are on the left. A is top-left, B bottom-left, and Mid crosses the centre from Garage (T) to Z Connector (CT). Ts reach A through the Long A hall and A Main, with Squeaky joining from Mid; they reach B through B Halls and B Main, with the Sun Room window facing B. CTs reach A along the west lane past the Truck or via Highway from Z, and B through Tree Room, the Heaven stairs and Checkers. Reported removals vs CS:GO: Z ladder/scaffolding; the Mid window is reported removed or reduced.

callouts.name: T Spawn
callouts.look: Open yard on the far right (east) of the radar with concrete, containers and warehouse walls.
callouts.use: Ts start here. Exits: north-west to the Long A yard, west into Garage for Mid, south-west to B Halls.

callouts.name: Garage
callouts.look: Large T-side warehouse between T Spawn and Mid with a long vehicle inside; a white column stands at its T-side door.
callouts.use: Ts' safe route into Mid. Valve's 'White Box' smoke is thrown from its T-side door ('push into the middle of the white column'). CTs pre-aim its Mid exit from Z.

callouts.name: Long A
callouts.look: Hall/yard north of Garage that runs up toward A, with side rooms on the right; Valve's 'Cross' smoke is thrown from a corner at its north end.
callouts.use: T staging area for A. Valve's retake file names this hall 'Long A' and the yard at its south end 'A Main'; the game's place list also has 'Outside A' and 'A Halls' (exact areas unconfirmed).

callouts.name: Squeaky
callouts.look: Doorway at the south end of A Main where Mid, the Long A yard and A Main meet (red hatched block on the radar).
callouts.use: Link that lets Ts in Mid join A Main. Moving through it gives a sound cue; CTs on A and in Mid listen for it. Official place name 'Squeaky'.

callouts.name: A Main
callouts.look: Narrow corridor running north from Squeaky to the A site entrance; the exit opens onto the east side of A beside the forklift.
callouts.use: Main T entry to A. Valve's CT 'A Main' smoke (thrown from the Truck) lands at its exit; CTs hold it from Quad, Truck and Toxic.

callouts.name: Forklift
callouts.look: Forklift and a crate at the south-east of A, next to the A Main exit.
callouts.use: Close cover for Ts entering A and for CT close holds; named 'Fork' in Valve's retake file. Common post-plant spot.

callouts.name: Quad
callouts.look: Stack of crates at the back (north-west) of A site.
callouts.use: CT hold facing the A Main exit across the site and a T post-plant spot; molotov or HE it before planting.

callouts.name: Blue Door
callouts.look: Blue door in the north wall of A (named 'Outside Blue Door' in Valve's retake file).
callouts.use: Extra hiding spot/entry at the back of A. Check it when clearing the site; patch notes mention clipping fixes around blue doors.

callouts.name: A Site
callouts.look: Open concrete yard top-left with crates, a green crate, the Quad stack at the back, the forklift by A Main and the truck lane to the west.
callouts.use: Bomb site A. Ts enter from A Main; CTs from the Truck lane and Highway. Plants named by Valve: default, 'for A Main', 'green crate', 'highway/truck', 'middle of site'.

callouts.name: Catwalk
callouts.look: Raised walkway along the south edge of A above the Toxic barrels (hatched strip on the radar).
callouts.use: Elevated spot over A named in Valve's retake file; a T post-plant or CT off-angle that needs checking.

callouts.name: Toxic
callouts.look: Hazard (toxic) barrels at the south-west corner of A where Highway arrives.
callouts.use: CT spot that watches the A Main exit across the site and a T post-plant spot facing Highway.

callouts.name: Truck
callouts.look: Large truck parked in the lane west of A on the CT side.
callouts.use: CT cover on the CT Spawn route to A. Valve's CT 'A Main' smoke is thrown from here; Ts' 'Cross' smoke blocks this side.

callouts.name: Highway
callouts.look: Corridor running south from the south-west corner of A to Z Connector.
callouts.use: CT rotation path between Mid and A and the Mid player's link to A; Ts who win Mid can flank A through it.

callouts.name: CT Spawn
callouts.look: Building and yard on the far left (west) of the radar; the spawn opens to the south.
callouts.use: CTs start here. Routes: north along the Truck lane to A, east to Z Connector, south-east through Tree Room to B.

callouts.name: Z Connector
callouts.look: Z-shaped corridor between Mid, Highway and the CT side.
callouts.use: CT control point for Mid and the hub between A and B. Valve's 'Connector' smoke, thrown from the yard north of Garage, blinds it so Ts can take Mid. The CS:GO Z ladder and scaffolding are reported removed.

callouts.name: Mid
callouts.look: Wide open yard across the centre with a white box, a large grey container and Squeaky on its north side.
callouts.use: Central control zone. Whoever owns Mid can split to A via Squeaky or Highway and to B via Checkers.

callouts.name: White Box
callouts.look: White box/structure in the middle of Mid.
callouts.use: Main T smoke target in Mid (Valve 'White Box' smoke from Garage) to block CT views from Z and Highway while Ts cross.

callouts.name: Checkers
callouts.look: Corridor between Mid and the north side of B, next to the Heaven stairs.
callouts.use: CT route from Mid to B and a T route from Mid onto B. Reported CS2 change: a self-boost at back Checkers.

callouts.name: Heaven
callouts.look: Raised platform at the north side of B reached by stairs, with a panel on its wall.
callouts.use: Strong CT hold over B and B Main; Valve's 'B Main' smoke is thrown from here. Ts block it with Valve's 'Heaven' smoke from Sun Room.

callouts.name: Hell
callouts.look: Ground area under Heaven at the north side of B.
callouts.use: Close CT hold and T post-plant spot; check it when entering B.

callouts.name: Tree Room
callouts.look: Room on the west (CT) side of B; Valve's 'Tree' smoke lands at its exit onto B.
callouts.use: CT entry to B from CT Spawn and the main retake route. Ts smoke it to cut rotations. Official place name 'Tree Room'.

callouts.name: Headshot
callouts.look: Low cover on the west side of B where a defender shows only the head.
callouts.use: CT angle onto the B Main entrance; T post-plant spot. Official place name 'Headshot'.

callouts.name: Back of Site
callouts.look: Rear (south-west) corner of B behind the site crates.
callouts.use: CT hide spot and a T post-plant spot; molotov it before planting.

callouts.name: B Site
callouts.look: Bottom-left site with crates, open to B Main on the east, Heaven and Hell on the north and Tree Room on the west.
callouts.use: Bomb site B. Plants named by Valve: default, 'behind default', 'back site', 'top of ramp'.

callouts.name: B Main
callouts.look: Long hall from B Halls west to the B site entrance.
callouts.use: Main T route to B. CTs hold it from Heaven, Headshot and the site; Valve's CT 'B Main' smoke from Heaven lands here.

callouts.name: Sun Room
callouts.look: Small room south of B Main with a sun painting and a window toward B; posts frame the window.
callouts.use: T utility room: Valve's 'Tree' and 'Heaven' smokes are thrown from here. Ts can also peek B through the window.

callouts.name: B Halls
callouts.look: Corridor from T Spawn toward B Main and Sun Room.
callouts.use: T staging area for B; CTs who push B Main early meet Ts here. Official place name 'B Halls'.
