mechanics.name: Price, damage and radius
mechanics.detail: An HE costs $300. Its base damage is 99 and its radius is 350 units (weapons.vdata). The server multipliers for damage and radius are both 1. A kill pays $300.

mechanics.name: Fuse
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code the HE bursts 1.5 s after the throw, even mid-air. CS2 has not published its fuse.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Falloff with distance
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code damage falls on a bell curve: full at the centre, about 84% at 70 units, 49% at 140, 20% at 210, 6% at 280 and 1% at 350. Walls that hide part of you cut it further.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Damage through armour
mechanics.detail: The HE's armour ratio in weapons.vdata is 1.2, which under the armour formula sends about 60% to health: up to about 59 at point blank, against 99 unarmoured. Guides quote 98 unarmoured and 57 armoured (57.5%).
mechanics.reason: File-based formula (60%) and guides (57.5%) differ slightly; Valve has not published HE armour damage.

mechanics.name: Mid-air bursts (Jan 2026)
mechanics.detail: Since 30 Jan 2026 an HE that bursts in the air near the ground no longer deals damage as if it had burst on the ground. Damage now uses the real burst point.

mechanics.name: Clears smoke
mechanics.detail: An HE blows a short-lived hole in a smoke, and since Oct 2024 it also clears the grey screen for players inside near the blast.

mechanics.name: Teammate and self damage
mechanics.detail: In Competitive, teammates take 85% of your HE damage (ff_damage_reduction_grenade 0.85). Your own HE hurts you in full.

mechanics.name: Stack HEs with teammates
mechanics.detail: Two HEs landing on one spot at point blank can kill a full-health armoured player (about 114 total). Three make it more reliable at range. Count down and throw together.

mechanics.name: Damage before the fight
mechanics.detail: Land an HE on a common hold before the swing. A player on 40 health dies to two AK body shots instead of four.

mechanics.name: Open a smoke
mechanics.detail: Throw an HE into the smoke you need to see through, then peek during the short gap.

mechanics.name: Post-plant and retake damage
mechanics.detail: An HE on the defuser, or on players hiding in a retake corner, adds damage and slows them a little.

mechanics.name: Throwing it at nobody
mechanics.detail: An HE far from players does little: in CS:GO code it is down to about a fifth at 210 units. Throw it at a known or likely position.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Hitting your own team
mechanics.detail: Teammates take 85% of HE damage in Competitive. Do not throw it where your entry will be.

mechanics.name: Dying with it
mechanics.detail: An unused HE is money lost. Use it before a risky fight or pass it to a teammate.

arsenal.name: Flashbang

stats.blindSeconds: up to about 5 at full flash (community)

arsenal.summary: Blinds players who look towards it when it pops, for up to a few seconds depending on angle and distance. Up to 2 per player in Competitive.
strengths: Wins entry duels when the enemy is blinded
Pop-flashes over walls are hard to dodge
weaknesses: Visible arc gives away your push if thrown early
counters: Turn away or hide behind a wall when you hear or see it
Re-peek after the flash wears off
tips: Throw it so it pops just as it clears the wall (pop-flash).
Call your flashes so teammates turn away.
Swing the moment it pops; the blind fades quickly.
arsenal.look: Kill feed and HUD: small cylindrical grenade. On screen the world turns white when you are flashed; the GSI field player.state.flashed goes up to 255.

mechanics.name: Price and carry limit
mechanics.detail: A flashbang costs $200. In Competitive you can carry two flashes inside the four-grenade total (ammo_grenade_limit_flashbang 2).

mechanics.name: Fuse
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code a flash bursts 1.5 s after it leaves the hand, in the air or on the ground. CS2 keeps a time-to-detonate field for the flash, but the value is not published.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: What decides how blind you are
mechanics.detail: Three things: distance to the burst, the angle between your view and the flash, and whether walls hide it. CS2's server still applies a hold time of full white, then a fade.

mechanics.name: Blind formula in CS:GO code, part 1
mechanics.detail: Strength falls in a straight line from full at the burst to zero at 3000 units. Other players do not shield you. If walls block the direct line to your eyes, three side checks each give 16.7% strength.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Blind formula in CS:GO code, part 2
mechanics.detail: Facing within about 53 degrees gives the full effect; 53 to 72 degrees about 65 to 70%; 72 to 101 degrees about 40%; turned further away about 20%. Both the solid-white hold and the fade scale this way.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Longest blinds
mechanics.detail: Demo data puts a close, full-face CS2 flash near 5.5 s of the game's flash-duration value, with real white time up to about 5 s. A CS:GO table gives up to 4.87 s in total with about 1.88 s of solid white. Guides quote 3 to 5 s.
mechanics.reason: Single demo-based figure for CS2; the table is CS:GO only.

mechanics.name: Full blind versus partial
mechanics.detail: The kill feed shows a blind kill when the killer was at least 70% flashed (sv_flashed_amount_for_blind_kill 0.7); Valve tuned this in Dec 2024. Since Nov 2024 the arm-over-eyes pose shows only when a player is fully blind.

mechanics.name: White-out, after-image and ringing
mechanics.detail: A flash gives a white screen, a fading after-image of the moment it burst, and ringing ears. CS2 has long, medium and short ring sounds. Valve's item text says the bang also masks footsteps.

mechanics.name: Ringing distances in CS:GO code
mechanics.detail: CS:GO picked the ring strength by distance: under 100 units, under 500 and under 1000.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Teammates and yourself
mechanics.detail: A flash blinds anyone who sees it, your team and you included. The game counts teammates hit, and the kill feed credits flash assists.

mechanics.name: Flashes and smoke
mechanics.detail: A smoke does not stop a flash from blinding a player inside or behind it. Flashes also light up the cloud.
mechanics.reason: Guides only; Valve has not documented flash and smoke interaction.

mechanics.name: Pop flash
mechanics.detail: Throw it so it bursts the moment it clears the wall or corner, often off a wall or over the top. The enemy gets almost no time to turn away. If it pops early they wait it out.

mechanics.name: Flash for a teammate
mechanics.detail: Stand behind or beside the peeker, say the flash and the count, and let them swing on the pop. The thrower aims so it bursts in the enemy's view and behind the peeker's eyes.

mechanics.name: Self-flash when peeking
mechanics.detail: Right-click or medium-throw a flash round the corner, then peek as it pops. It is fast and needs no partner, but your own timing must be exact.

mechanics.name: Trading flash
mechanics.detail: When your entry dies, flash the killer's spot at once so the next player can trade while the killer is blind or turned away.

mechanics.name: Turning away
mechanics.detail: When you hear or see an enemy flash, turn well away (over about 100 degrees) or break line of sight. In CS:GO code this cut the effect to about a fifth.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Retake flashes
mechanics.detail: CTs should keep flashes for the retake: flash the planted site from cover and swing together. A credible retake needs utility.

mechanics.name: Track your flash value
mechanics.detail: Leetify recaps rank about 0.65 enemies blinded per flash as above average and about 0.85 as top few percent. Aim to blind enemies, not teammates.
mechanics.reason: Benchmarks inferred from individual Leetify recap pages, not an official threshold.

mechanics.name: Team-flashing
mechanics.detail: Flat throws that burst behind your own peeker blind the team. Call 'flashing' and the spot so they turn, and throw high so it bursts in front of them.

mechanics.name: Pop timing off
mechanics.detail: A flash that pops before the enemy can see it, or after your teammate has swung, does nothing. Practise the count.

mechanics.name: Flashing with no one to peek
mechanics.detail: A flash nobody plays off is $200 wasted. Only throw it when someone is ready to swing.

mechanics.name: Peeking while blind
mechanics.detail: Wait out a flash behind cover. A blind player rarely wins the duel, and the kill feed shows it when one does.

arsenal.name: Smoke Grenade
arsenal.summary: Creates a volumetric smoke cloud that blocks vision. CS2 smokes fill the space, can be briefly cleared by an HE or pierced by bullets, and put out molotov and incendiary fires.
strengths: Cuts off sightlines for site takes and retakes
weaknesses: HE grenades and gunfire can open gaps
counters: Throw an HE to open a gap, then shoot through
Hold the exit of the smoke
tips: Learn one default smoke per site for each side.
Smoke the defender's best angle, not the doorway you walk through.
Use a smoke to stop a molotov burning you out.
arsenal.look: Kill feed: tall can-shaped grenade. On screen: a grey cloud; kills through it show the through-smoke icon in the kill feed.

mechanics.name: Price, slot and kill reward
mechanics.detail: A smoke costs $300 and takes one grenade slot. In Competitive you can carry one smoke. Like every grenade, a kill with it pays $300.

mechanics.name: It pops once it stops moving
mechanics.detail: A smoke does not burst on a set timer. It waits until it has come to rest. Since Nov 2023 it also has a minimum fuse, so a smoke stuck in a gap no longer pops too early.

mechanics.name: Fuse timing in CS:GO code
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code the smoke first checked 1.5 s after the throw, then every 0.2 s, and burst once its speed was close to zero. CS2's minimum fuse value is not published.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: How long the cloud lasts
mechanics.detail: CS2 demo data shows about 22 s from the pop to the smoke-expired event, which that source splits into about 18 s of full cover and 4 s of fade. Guides quote 15 to 20 s. Coach it as about 18 s of solid cover.
mechanics.reason: The 22 s split is one non-official demo measurement; Valve has not published a duration and guides disagree.

mechanics.name: A volumetric cloud that fills the space
mechanics.detail: CS2 smokes are a 3D volume, not a flat sprite. The cloud spreads to fill rooms, flows round boxes and through doors and windows, so the same throw can look different in two places. The server sends the same cloud to every player.

mechanics.name: HE grenades blow a hole in it
mechanics.detail: Valve's own buy-menu tip for the HE says it can clear smoke. An HE that bursts in or next to the cloud pushes it aside, then the smoke flows back. Since Oct 2024 it also clears the grey screen effect for players inside the smoke near the blast.

mechanics.name: How long an HE hole stays open
mechanics.detail: Valve gives no figure. One article puts the gap at about 3 s before the smoke refills. Treat it as a short window of a few seconds and peek with it, not after it.
mechanics.reason: Single non-official source; no Valve figure.

mechanics.name: Bullets thin it
mechanics.detail: Gunfire punches short-lived holes in the cloud, so heavy spraying can open a lane for a moment. The kill feed flags kills made through smoke (the thrusmoke field in the death event).

mechanics.name: Smoke puts out fire: the one-third rule
mechanics.detail: A smoke that blooms over a molotov or incendiary puts it out. The CS2 server ends the whole fire once more than a third of its fire areas are covered by smoke. Valve fixed overlapping-smoke cases in Aug and Oct 2025.

mechanics.name: Fire cannot spread into smoke
mechanics.detail: Flames do not spread into an active smoke, and a molotov that bursts inside a smoke fizzles out. A smoke that lands on burning fire pops at once. CS2 keeps the schema flags for both cases.

mechanics.name: Inside the smoke
mechanics.detail: Standing in the cloud greys out your screen, and players can still shoot through it. Offline bots see players through up to 200 units of smoke (bot_max_visible_smoke_length 200).

mechanics.name: Bomb blast now clears smoke (Jul 2026)
mechanics.detail: Since 20 Jul 2026 the C4 explosion interacts with smoke clouds and fire. Reports say it clears smoke for a few seconds like an HE and puts out molotov fire inside the blast.

mechanics.name: Give every smoke a job
mechanics.detail: A smoke should cut one sightline: an AWP lane, a cross, or a defender's angle on your entry. Valve's own tip is to throw it to cut off enemy line of sight. Name the job before you throw.

mechanics.name: Time smokes to the execute
mechanics.detail: Throw execute smokes so they bloom just before the team moves. Too early and defenders wait it out; too late and the angle is lost. With about 18 s of cover, the hit must follow within seconds.

mechanics.name: Deep and shallow smokes
mechanics.detail: A deep smoke lands near the defenders' spot, so it blocks them at the source and lets your team take more ground. A shallow smoke lands close to you: safer to land, but enemies can wait at its edge. Many spots have both versions.

mechanics.name: One-way smokes in CS2
mechanics.detail: Classic one-ways mostly stopped working, since both sides see one shared volume. Thin edges and gaps under ledges can still give one side a partial view. Valve has fixed several one-way cases, so use them as a bonus, not a plan.
mechanics.reason: Guides only; Valve keeps patching edge cases, so current behaviour may differ by spot.

mechanics.name: Save a smoke for the defuse
mechanics.detail: On CT, keep one smoke for the post-plant. It puts out a molotov on the bomb so the kit holder can defuse, and it hides the defuser from long angles.

mechanics.name: Smoke plus flash
mechanics.detail: A smoke and a flash into the same space is a strong pair: the smoke blocks the angle and the flash still blinds anyone who waits inside or behind it.
mechanics.reason: Flash-through-smoke behaviour is from guides; Valve has not described it.

mechanics.name: Learn Valve's starter smokes
mechanics.detail: Valve's official map guides teach four to seven standard smokes per map, with stand spot, aim point and landing spot. They are the quickest way to a reliable default set.

mechanics.name: Do not empty a magazine into smoke
mechanics.detail: Since Mar 2026 a reload throws away the bullets left in the magazine. Spraying blind into smoke now costs reserve ammo. m0NESY said the change should cut useless smoke spamming.

mechanics.name: Smoking your own team off
mechanics.detail: A smoke that lands on your own entry path or blocks your AWP's lane helps the defenders. Check where teammates will peek before you throw.

mechanics.name: Smoke too early or too late
mechanics.detail: An early smoke fades before the hit; a late one lands after the fight. Count from the throw, not from the pop.

mechanics.name: Peeking from the smoke edge
mechanics.detail: Players can show at the thin edge of a cloud. Valve adjusted silhouettes in smoke in Feb 2024. Step out fully or hold back, do not hover at the edge.

mechanics.name: Molly into your own smoke
mechanics.detail: A molotov or incendiary thrown into an active smoke fizzles. Throw the fire first, or into a different spot.

mechanics.name: Old lineups on slopes
mechanics.detail: Animgraph 2 (live from 20 Apr 2026) changed player height on sloped ground, so lineups thrown from slopes may now land elsewhere. Valve adjusted its own guides on 24 Apr 2026. Re-check old lineups.

arsenal.name: Molotov
arsenal.summary: Terrorist fire grenade. Bursts into flames on impact with the floor (or after about 2 s in the air) and burns an area for about 7 s, dealing 40 damage per second. Denies corners and forces players out.
strengths: Clears close corners and default plant spots
weaknesses: Visible and avoidable if thrown early
counters: Smoke the fire or wait it out from a safe angle
tips: Molotov the CT's close corner before entering a site.
After planting, save one to stop the defuse.
Bounce it off walls to reach deep corners.
arsenal.look: Kill feed: bottle with a burning rag. On screen: orange fire patch on the ground; the GSI field player.state.burning rises when you stand in fire.
arsenal.notes: Flame lifetime 7 s average, 40 damage per second, spread 150 units, 2 s air detonation, all from game convars.

mechanics.name: Price, side and slot
mechanics.detail: The molotov costs $400 and is the Terrorist fire grenade. It shares an ammo type with the incendiary, so you carry one fire grenade at most. A kill pays $300.

mechanics.name: When it bursts
mechanics.detail: It bursts when it hits ground no steeper than 30 degrees; walls make it bounce. If it never touches the world it air-bursts after 2 s (molotov_throw_detonate_time 2).

mechanics.name: Bounce off an enemy (Jan 2026)
mechanics.detail: Since 27 Jan 2026 a molotov or incendiary that bounces off an enemy gets a one-time fuse extension, so it does not air-burst early.

mechanics.name: Burn time and spread
mechanics.detail: Each flame lives about 7 s (inferno_flame_lifetime 7). Fire spreads up to 150 units from where it landed, with up to 16 flames. Demo data shows molotovs burn about 7.0 s.

mechanics.name: Damage
mechanics.detail: Fire deals 40 damage per second (inferno_damage 40), applied every 0.2 s, so 8 per tick.

mechanics.name: Damage ramp in CS:GO code
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code fire damage rose from zero to full over the first 2 s after it landed. CS2 still has a damage-ramp timer in its fire entity.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Armour and fire
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code armour did not reduce burn damage; it only applied to bullets, blasts and knives. CS2's file still lists an armour ratio for the molotov, so this is not confirmed.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: Teammate fire
mechanics.detail: In CS:GO code a teammate's fire counted as 'other' friendly damage. Competitive sets that to 40% (ff_damage_reduction_other 0.4). Your own fire hurts you in full.
mechanics.reason: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.

mechanics.name: How to put it out
mechanics.detail: A smoke puts it out once it covers over a third of the fire. Since Jul 2026 the C4 blast also puts out fire inside it. Fire cannot spread into smoke.

mechanics.name: Flame pillar
mechanics.detail: Since May 2024 the tall pillar of flame gets shorter over time, so late in the burn it blocks less view.

mechanics.name: Clear a corner
mechanics.detail: Burn a close hiding spot before you walk past it. Valve's tip: clear out hiding spots with fire and throw it before attacking a bombsite.

mechanics.name: Stop a defuse
mechanics.detail: A fresh molotov on the bomb makes even a 5 s kit defuse deadly for a full-health player at 40 damage a second, unless the CT smokes it. Throw it when you hear the defuse start, from a safe lineup.

mechanics.name: Delay a push or rotation
mechanics.detail: Fire on a choke buys about 7 s. Ts use it to stop a flank or a CT push into the site.

mechanics.name: Pair it with an HE
mechanics.detail: Fire forces players to move; an HE on the spot they move to adds damage.

mechanics.name: Throwing into smoke
mechanics.detail: It fizzles in an active smoke. Burn first, then smoke, or pick another spot.

mechanics.name: Hitting a wall
mechanics.detail: A wall or steep slope makes it bounce, often back towards you. Aim for flat ground.

mechanics.name: Burning your own path
mechanics.detail: Do not burn the corridor your team must walk through in the next 7 s.

mechanics.name: Running through fire
mechanics.detail: Fire deals 40 damage a second. Wait it out, smoke it or find another route.

arsenal.name: Incendiary Grenade
arsenal.summary: CT fire grenade ($500 since 2024). In CS2 it spreads faster but burns a smaller area for less time than the molotov: about 5.5 s and 110 units, at 40 damage per second.
strengths: Stops a rush or a plant quickly
weaknesses: Shorter and smaller than the Terrorist molotov
counters: Smoke it or wait it out
tips: Throw it at the entry point when you hear the push.
Use it to delay a plant while teammates rotate.
arsenal.look: Kill feed: cylindrical grenade with a flame. On screen: fire patch like the molotov.
arsenal.notes: Values from game convars inferno_flame_lifetime_incendiary 5.5 and inferno_max_range_ct 110 (inferno_ct_experiment on).

mechanics.name: Price and side
mechanics.detail: The incendiary is the CT fire grenade and costs $500, cut from $600 in May 2024. It shares the fire slot with the molotov. A kill pays $300.

mechanics.name: Shorter, smaller, faster
mechanics.detail: Each flame lives about 5.5 s (molotov 7 s). It spreads up to 110 units (molotov 150) but ten times faster (inferno_spread_speed_mult_ct 10). Valve made it spread faster in Jul 2025.

mechanics.name: Same damage and fuse as the molotov
mechanics.detail: 40 damage per second, a 2 s air-burst if it never lands, and it only bursts on ground up to 30 degrees.

mechanics.name: Putting it out
mechanics.detail: Smoke over more than a third of the fire ends it. The C4 blast also puts it out since Jul 2026.

mechanics.name: Stop a rush at a choke
mechanics.detail: Valve's tip: it stifles enemy attacks, so throw it at the first sign of trouble. It covers its area almost at once.

mechanics.name: Anchor's stall tool
mechanics.detail: An anchor holds a site alone longer with an incendiary on the main entrance while rotations arrive.

mechanics.name: Deny a plant
mechanics.detail: Burning the usual plant spot forces Ts to plant elsewhere or wait.

mechanics.name: Throwing too early
mechanics.detail: It lasts only about 5.5 s. Thrown before the push commits, it burns out before they arrive.

mechanics.name: Into a smoke
mechanics.detail: It fizzles in an active smoke, the same as a molotov.

mechanics.name: Dying with it
mechanics.detail: A held incendiary does nothing. Use it on the first real push.

arsenal.name: Decoy Grenade
arsenal.summary: Plays fake gunfire of your weapon where it lands. Cheap way to fake presence; small damage when it finally pops.
strengths: Can draw attention or fake a site
counters: Check the radar and sound; ignore fake shots that do not move
tips: Use it on ecos as a cheap distraction.
Throw it at a site while your team hits the other.
arsenal.look: Kill feed: small grenade icon. On screen: a small device on the floor firing sound effects.

mechanics.name: What it does
mechanics.detail: A $50 grenade that plays the gunfire sound of the most powerful weapon you carry. Valve says it also affects the enemy minimap.

mechanics.name: Timing
mechanics.detail: It starts once it stops moving and plays bursts for about 15 s, then pops. CS:GO code used a 2 s timer and 14 s of shots.
mechanics.reason: 15 s comes from guides and CS:GO code; Valve has not published the CS2 value.

mechanics.name: Damage
mechanics.detail: Sources disagree on the final pop: one guide lists 0 damage, while CS:GO code used 25 within about 88 units. In CS2 it does not hurt teammates (ff_damage_decoy_explosion false).
mechanics.reason: Guides disagree on damage; 25 is the CS:GO value.

mechanics.name: Smoke interaction
mechanics.detail: Since Nov 2023 decoys interact visually with smoke clouds.

mechanics.name: Fake a player or an AWP
mechanics.detail: Throw it where you want the enemy to think a player is. It plays your best gun, so with an AWP in your loadout it sounds like an AWP.

mechanics.name: Cheap fourth grenade
mechanics.detail: At $50 it can fill the last slot when money is tight, but a flash is usually worth more.

mechanics.name: Obvious fakes
mechanics.detail: Decoys fire in bursts with pauses, and good players know the sound. Use it with real pressure elsewhere.
mechanics.reason: Burst pattern is from CS:GO code.

mechanics.name: Buying it over a flash
mechanics.detail: With money for a full set, a flash or smoke does more than a decoy.

arsenal.name: Kevlar Vest
arsenal.summary: Body armour (100 points). Reduces damage to the chest, stomach and arms by each weapon's armour penetration and reduces aim punch. Does not protect the head.
strengths: Cheapest armour; key on pistol rounds
Cuts damage from SMGs and pistols
weaknesses: No head protection: P250, USP-S and Glock headshots still one-shot
counters: Aim for the head against vest-only players
tips: Ts often buy Kevlar on the pistol round; CTs often split Kevlar and a kit.
On force buys, Kevlar first, then guns.
arsenal.look: HUD: shield icon next to health with the armour number; no helmet outline. GSI: player.state.armor > 0 and helmet false.

arsenal.name: Kevlar + Helmet
arsenal.summary: Full armour: vest plus helmet. The helmet stops one-shot headshots from most pistols, SMGs and the M4s. Standard on every full buy.
weaknesses: Does not stop AK-47, SG 553, Desert Eagle, snipers or close Tec-9/Five-SeveN one-shots
counters: Use AK-47, Deagle or snipers against helmeted players
tips: Buy it every full buy; on second rounds it decides many fights.
If money is short, a teammate can drop you a weapon so you can afford the helmet.
arsenal.look: HUD: shield icon with a helmet outline next to health. GSI: player.state.helmet true.
arsenal.notes: Helmet upgrade price for players who already own a full vest is community knowledge ($350).

arsenal.name: Defuse Kit
arsenal.summary: CT-only kit that halves the defuse time from 10 s to 5 s. Drops on death; since 8 Oct 2026 a dropped kit shows a ping icon.
strengths: Lets you defuse after the first enemy dies
counters: Ts: kill the kit holder first or deny the defuse with fire
tips: At least two CTs should carry kits on full buys.
Pick up dropped kits on retakes.
arsenal.look: HUD: pliers icon on the player; top-centre avatars show a kit icon. Radar: a kit icon where one is dropped. GSI: player.state.defusekit.

arsenal.name: Zeus x27
arsenal.summary: Taser that kills in one hit at very close range. Kill reward $100. In CS2 it recharges about 30 s after use; up to 5 can be bought per round in Competitive.
weaknesses: Very short range (game data range 120 units)
counters: Keep distance from players holding it
tips: Hold a tight corner on a site with it for a surprise kill.
Do not rely on it in open fights.
arsenal.look: Kill feed: small taser with a lightning bolt. First person: yellow-and-black taser.

items.name: Game identity
items.detail: Counter-Strike 2 (CS2), Valve, Source 2 engine. Released 27 September 2023 as the free-to-play replacement for CS:GO on Steam. Runs on Windows and Linux (no macOS client). 5v5 tactical shooter: Terrorists (T) plant the bomb on site A or B; Counter-Terrorists (CT) prevent or defuse it. Money earned each round buys weapons, armour and grenades.

items.name: Current build
items.detail: Game files list PatchVersion 1.41.9.2 dated Oct 22 2026 (steam.inf, SteamDatabase mirror). Small October 2026 updates were reported (one outlet: faster AUG reload and a ping icon for dropped defuse kits on Oct 8; unverified, not read from Valve notes).

items.name: Premier season
items.detail: Premier Season Five began in July 2026 (Valve notes date it 8 July; some sites say 6 July). Season medals need 25 Premier wins and an active CS Rating at season end (game UI text).

items.name: 2026 changes, first half
items.detail: March 18 2026: reload rework (a reload drops the current magazine and its bullets; reserve counted in magazines). July 8 2026: Premier Season Five, Cache in and Overpass out of Active Duty, bomb explosion redesign with damage baked per map. July 20/21 2026: the bomb blast clears smoke and puts out fire; the health-bar bomb damage preview shows only once the bomb is audible.

items.name: 2026 changes, second half
items.detail: Sept 22/23 2026 "Rush Hour": Rush 3v3 mode, Premier map picks instead of bans, silent reload (hold the key) and silent unscope, crosshair changes. Sept 25 fix added half outlines for crosshairs.

items.name: Game State Integration
items.detail: Valve's official Game State Integration (GSI) sends JSON to a local endpoint set in a cfg file: map, round phase, scores, bomb state, and for the local player health, armour, helmet, money, equipment value, weapons and ammo, round kills and headshot kills, and flashed, smoked and burning levels (0 to 255). Field names follow the Valve wiki page written for CS:GO (not re-checked for CS2).

items.name: Coaching policy note
items.detail: Sightline coaches live only offline or against bots; Premier, Competitive and other online matches get post-match coaching only. The coach reads the screen and Valve Game State Integration and never touches game memory or input.

items.name: Update 2026-01-21
items.detail: Anubis (reworked) returned to Active Duty; Train left the pool.; MP7: price $1,500 to $1,400, damage 29 to 30, range modifier 0.85 to 0.87 (less fall-off).; MP5-SD: price $1,500 to $1,400, damage 27 to 28, range modifier 0.85 to 0.87.; PP-Bizon: price $1,400 to $1,300 (no damage change).; Jump landing now uses sub-tick timing.

items.name: Update 2026-03-18
items.detail: ; Reserve ammo is now counted in magazines and retuned per weapon (for example AWP 2 spare magazines = 15 shots per round; AK-47 3; M4A4 4 = +30 rounds; Galil AR 4 = +50 rounds). ; Limited in-game map guides (annotations) in Competitive and Retakes for the first 5 rounds of each half (sv_allow_annotations_access_level 1, sv_annotation_limits_max_rounds_per_half 5).

items.name: Update 2026-03-18 (2)
items.detail: ; Friends can join Practice and Workshop map sessions from the friends list when Open Party is on.

items.name: Update 2026-07-06

items.name: Update 2026-09-22
items.detail: ; Silent reload: hold the reload key to reload quietly but slowly. ; Crosshair overhaul: new Settings section Crosshair / Scopes, new styles, default style is now Dynamic Quad (cl_crosshairstyle 7); older crosshair codes were reported invalid. ; Clan tags returned; the Zeus x27 now hurts chickens; per-mode music volume settings.

items.name: Update 2026-10-22
items.detail: New voice-chat audio processing options (WebRTC echo cancellation, gain control, noise suppression convars). Read from game files; no gameplay, HUD or economy change found.

items.name: Premier
items.detail: 5v5, MR12 (first to 13 of 24 rounds) with overtime, CS Rating (numbers, colour tiers). Since Sept 22/23 2026 a pick system replaced bans: Team 1 picks one map, Team 2 picks two, Team 1 picks a fourth, and one of the four is chosen at random. Active Duty pool only. A July 2026 update reportedly allowed 4-player premades (unverified).

items.name: Competitive
items.detail: 5v5 on a chosen map (or maps) with a Skill Group per map. MR12; a 12-12 score ends as a draw (no overtime by default, per guides). Settings in the Oct 2026 config: $800 start, $16,000 cap, 1:55 rounds, 15 s freeze time, 20 s buy time, friendly fire on (bullets do 33 percent to teammates), team collision on, Killer Replay off.

items.name: Wingman
items.detail: 2v2 on small maps, best of 16 rounds, $8,000 money cap, 1:30 rounds, 10 s freeze time, loss bonus $2,000 plus $300 per loss, Killer Replay off (Wingman config). Wingman map group in the game files: Debris, Eldorado, Poseidon, Overpass, Vertigo, Nuke, Inferno (display names unverified).

items.name: Casual
items.detail: 10v10, friendly fire off, team collision off, 50 percent kill rewards, best of 15 (game UI text). Good for relaxed practice; not representative of competitive economy.

items.name: Deathmatch
items.detail: Instant respawn, weapon chosen at spawn, 10-minute matches, points per kill. Used for aim warm-up.

items.name: Arms Race
items.detail: Gun-game: each kill upgrades your weapon; first to a Golden Knife kill wins. Instant respawn.

items.name: Retakes
items.detail: Official mode added October 2025: the bomb is already planted and CTs retake the site with set loadouts. Good practice for retakes and post-plants.

items.name: Rush
items.detail: Added Sept 2026: 3v3 through a gauntlet of battle arenas. Win a round by controlling the tower when time expires; win the match by capturing the enemy castle or winning 8 rounds (game UI text). Friendly fire on, armour purchasable.

items.name: Offline with bots / practice
items.detail: Local practice servers, workshop maps (aim_botz, Recoil Master, Yprac Hub prefire and utility maps) and offline matches with bots. This is where live coaching is allowed.

items.name: Active Duty pool (Premier Season Five, since July 2026)
items.detail: Ancient, Anubis, Cache, Dust II, Inferno, Mirage, Nuke. Cache returned for the first time in about seven years, replacing Overpass. The competitive map list in the Oct 2026 game files lists these seven first. Train left the pool earlier (one source says Anubis returned in its place on 22 January 2026; unverified).

items.name: Ancient
items.detail: Jungle temple map. Mid and the donut area connect to A; B is reached through a long ramp and cave. Guides call it CT-leaning; mid control is key.

items.name: Anubis
items.detail: Egyptian canal map with water in mid. Narrow chokes into both sites; the canal and connector make fast rotations for Ts.

items.name: Cache
items.detail: Industrial nuclear site map, reworked for 2026. Classic structure: A main, mid with Z-connector and highway, B main (squeaky door). Mid control splits the CTs. Exact 2026 rework callouts not verified here.

items.name: Dust II
items.detail: Desert classic: long A, short A (catwalk), mid doors and B tunnels. Long sightlines suit rifles and the AWP; mid control opens both sites.

items.name: Inferno
items.detail: Italian town: banana to B, apartments and short to A, mid. Close angles and heavy utility use; molotovs and smokes decide banana control.

items.name: Mirage
items.detail: Moroccan town: A ramp and palace to A, apartments to B, mid with window and connector. The most played map in Premier, per reports after the pick change.

items.name: Nuke
items.detail: Two sites stacked vertically (A upstairs, B below) with outside yard, ramp and vents. Fast CT rotations; guides call it CT-sided.

items.name: Reserve and other maps
items.detail: Overpass, Train and Vertigo are in reserve map groups in the game files; Office and Italy are hostage maps in Casual and Competitive.

items.name: Buy menu
items.detail: Opened in the buy zone during the freeze time and buy time (20 s in Competitive). Categories PISTOLS, SMGs, HEAVY, RIFLES, GEAR, GRENADES; weapon panels show COST, KILL AWARD, ARMOR PENETRATION, STOPPING POWER and more. Buttons: Re-Buy Previous, Auto Buy, Refund (sell back during buy time) and Hold to Buy and Throw (buy for a teammate).

items.name: Buy menu loadout
items.detail: A Dropped Weapons list shows nearby weapons. Which weapon fills each slot (M4A4 or M4A1-S, CZ75-Auto or Five-SeveN/Tec-9, Desert Eagle or R8, MP7 or MP5-SD) is set in the inventory loadout, so the menu differs between players.

items.name: Scoreboard (Tab)
items.detail: Per player: Money, K, A, D, MVPs (star), Score, HS%, ADR, KDR, UD (utility damage), EF (enemies flashed), DMG; a Loss Bonus column with a tooltip saying what your team will earn with a round loss. A Cycle Stats option shows extra columns. Teammates' money is visible; enemy money is not.

items.name: Round end
items.detail: Win panel with Terrorists Win or Counter-Terrorists Win and the reason: Bomb detonated, CTs eliminated, Bomb defused, Terrorists eliminated, or Bombing failed (time ran out), plus an MVP line (most eliminations, planting or defusing the bomb).

items.name: Round-end damage report
items.detail: Under the enemy portraits at the top of the screen the round-end report shows damage you gave (green fields) and took (dark fields) for each enemy. Guides say it is the only in-game damage readout in Competitive and Premier, and that it can be turned off (cl_disable_round_end_report, single source).

items.name: Death screen
items.detail: Competitive and Wingman have no Killer Replay (spec_replay_enable 0 in both configs). The view freezes briefly on the killer (spec_freeze_time 2 s) and the death panel appears: killer avatar with a health bar (their health left), killer name, "killed you with their <weapon>" and the weapon image. Then you spectate teammates only.

items.name: Death panel damage lines
items.detail: The Oct 2026 layout also has "Damage taken: X in N hits" and "Damage given: Y in N hits" rows with bars. Some players report damage no longer shows after death, so treat these rows as unverified until seen on screen.

items.name: Death panel special texts
items.detail: "You were killed by the C4 explosion", "You burned to death", "You were killed by your own grenade", "killed you with your own <weapon>" (killed with your dropped gun), "FINAL KILL of the round", and domination or revenge markers.

items.name: Killer Replay
items.detail: Exists in other modes (option Automatic Killer Replay; press Reload for Killer Replay). Off in Competitive and Wingman per the configs. When running, your player can be outlined.

items.name: Match end
items.detail: Final scoreboard and accolades such as The Executioner (most kills), The Pain Train (most damage), The Carry (highest ADR), The Bullseye (highest headshot percentage), The Tenderizer (most assists), The Trifecta and The Quad Killer (multi-kills). Premier shows the CS Rating change.

items.name: Halftime and overtime
items.detail: Sides swap after 12 rounds; money resets to $800 with the loss count at one. Overtime in Premier is played in 6-round blocks (3 per side); guides differ on start money ($10,000 default or $12,500).

items.name: Radar settings for the coach
items.detail: Make the radar a stable, north-up picture so the app can map icon pixels to map callouts and grid cells that match the official overview image. 00.

items.name: Kill feed
items.detail: Top right. Entry order: [eye icon if the killer was blind] killer [+ flashbang icon + assister, or + assister] [in-air icon] weapon [no-scope icon] [through-smoke icon] [wallbang icon] [headshot icon] victim. CT names blue, T names gold.

items.name: Kill feed: your entries
items.detail: Entries with you: your kills have a red outline, your deaths a dark red background. Entries last about 5 seconds, or 7.5 seconds when they involve you (game styles).

items.name: Radar
items.detail: Top left. Your arrow, teammates as coloured dots, enemies as red dots only when spotted by your team, the bomb (dropped, carried or planted) and bomb sites A and B.

items.name: Health and armour
items.detail: Bottom left: health (100 max) and armour value with a helmet icon when bought. Since July 2026 part of the health bar flashes red to preview bomb damage once the bomb is audible.

items.name: Weapon and ammo
items.detail: Bottom right: current weapon, bullets in the magazine and reserve. Since March 2026 reserve ammo is counted in magazines for most weapons.

items.name: Money
items.detail: Shown with the HUD during play and in the buy menu; teammates' money on the scoreboard. Max $16,000.

items.name: Team counter and timer
items.detail: Top centre: round timer between the two scores, player avatars per team (greyed when dead), or alive counts with the Large Player Count option. After the plant the timer is replaced by the bomb icon (no countdown is shown; players time it themselves).

items.name: Flash, smoke and fire
items.detail: A flash whites out the screen and fades; smoke appears as a grey cloud; fire shows flames and health loss. Game State Integration reports flashed, smoked and burning levels.

items.name: Damage indicator
items.detail: A red marker around the crosshair shows the direction of incoming damage.

items.name: Defuse and plant bars
items.detail: A progress bar appears while planting or defusing; a kit icon shows when a CT carries a defuse kit.

items.name: Options that change the look
items.detail: HUD scale, team overhead ID (When in View, or shown permanently with or without equipment), Large Player Count, crosshair style and outlines (half outlines since Sept 2026), round-end report on or off, Automatic Killer Replay. The vision model should not assume one fixed layout.

items.name: HUD: radar (top-left)
items.detail: Circular radar by default (about 250 px across inside a 300 px panel that starts about 40 px from the top, at 1080p). It turns square and shows the whole map while the Tab scoreboard is open (default) or at all times if Force Square Shape is on.

items.name: HUD: place name (directly under the radar, centred on it)
items.detail: Confirmed: CS2 shows the current place (callout) name of the local player under the radar as white text (radar layout element 'DashboardLabel', 22 px font). Names come from the map's navigation place names (for example 'Long Doors', 'BombsiteA').

items.name: HUD: team counter (top centre)
items.detail: Round timer (m:ss) in the middle with the CT score on its left and the T score on its right; player avatars for each team spread outwards (CT side left, T side right) with small health bars, dead players greyed with a skull; alive counts beside each team. Kill markers under an avatar show kills this round.

items.name: HUD: team counter (top centre) (2)
items.detail: During freeze time teammates' avatars can show money, best weapon, grenades, armour and kit. After a round, avatars show a damage report (damage given and taken).

items.name: HUD: bomb planted (top centre, in place of the timer)
items.detail: When the bomb is planted the timer is replaced by a red bomb icon with pulsing lines; there is no countdown number. A defused-bomb icon shows after a defuse. The planted bomb also appears on the radar.

items.name: HUD: money (bottom-left area, above the health and armour readout…
items.detail: Money as '$1,234' with a green shopping-cart icon while you are in the buy zone. Money gained flashes green, money spent flashes red. (Unverified.)

items.name: HUD: health armour (bottom-left)
items.detail: Health number with a cross icon and armour number with a shield icon (helmet outline when a helmet is worn), tinted by HUD Color (default: team colour).

items.name: HUD: ammo (bottom-right)
items.detail: Rounds in the magazine and reserve. Since Mar 2026 the reserve is shown as magazines, shells or bullets by weapon type, with a fill bar for the current magazine under the count.

items.name: HUD: inventory (right edge, lower half)
items.detail: Weapon list (primary, pistol, knife, grenades, C4) appears briefly when you switch weapons, or permanently with the inventory display setting in Settings > Game > Item (cl_showloadout 1).

items.name: HUD: kill feed (top-right, starting about 72 px from the top)
items.detail: Newest entry at the top; each lasts about 5 s (about 7.5 s if it involves you).

items.name: HUD: chat (lower-left, above the money)
items.detail: Team and all-chat messages and radio commands. (Unverified.)

items.name: HUD: centre messages (lower centre)
items.detail: Hint text, progress bars (planting and defusing), alerts.

items.name: HUD: win panel (upper centre, below the team counter)
items.detail: Round-end banner.

items.name: Radar 1
items.detail: Your own position: an arrow pointing where you look. With rotation on (default) the map turns and your arrow points up; with rotation off the map stays fixed and the arrow turns.

items.name: Radar 2
items.detail: Teammates: dots with a view cone. In Premier, Competitive and Wingman each teammate has a player colour (yellow, purple, green, blue or orange) that matches their avatar and scoreboard colour; with 'Colors and Letters' a letter is drawn too. In other modes teammates use the team colour (CT light blue, T yellow).

items.name: Radar 3
items.detail: Dead teammates: an X in their colour where they died.

items.name: Radar 4
items.detail: Enemies: a red dot (about #FF1919) while any player on your team can see them (spotted). When they leave sight a fading 'last seen' ghost marker remains briefly; you never see unspotted enemies.

items.name: Radar 5
items.detail: Dead enemies: a red X.

items.name: Radar 6
items.detail: Bomb: C4 icon on the carrier and where it is dropped (Terrorists see it; CTs see it once spotted, unverified). When planted, a bomb icon that flashes faster as detonation nears (three flash speeds in the layout).

items.name: Radar 7
items.detail: Bombsites: yellow 'A' and 'B' letters.

items.name: Radar 8
items.detail: Dropped defuse kit: kit icon (and a ping since 8 Oct 2026).

items.name: Radar 9
items.detail: Pings from teammates: expanding circles; speaking teammates: a green speaker icon on their dot.

items.name: Radar 10
items.detail: Teammates outside the visible radar area: arrows at the radar edge.

items.name: Radar 11
items.detail: Multi-level maps: small up or down markers on dots that are above or below your level.

items.name: Movement speeds
items.detail: Units per second, Oct 2026 data: knife 250; most pistols 240; MAC-10, MP9, PP-Bizon 240; P90 and UMP-45 230; M4A4 and M4A1-S 225; FAMAS and AUG 220; AK-47, Galil AR, XM1014 215; AWP 200 (100 scoped); Negev 150.

items.name: Accuracy and movement
items.detail: Inaccuracy rises steeply with speed: AK-47 0.0064 standing, 0.0048 crouching, 0.175 running; AWP 0.002 scoped standing, 0.176 moving. Community testing puts full accuracy below about 34 percent of a weapon's top speed. Counter-strafing (tapping the opposite key) stops you almost at once. Jumping shots are very inaccurate.

items.name: Recovery and recoil
items.detail: Spray adds inaccuracy that recovers over about 0.34 to 0.37 s for the main rifles when standing (AK-47 0.368 s, M4A4 0.339 s). Fire rate: AK-47 every 0.1 s (600 per minute), M4A4 every 0.09 s, M4A1-S every 0.1 s, AWP 1.455 s between shots. Recoil patterns are fixed per weapon and learnable.

items.name: Damage multipliers
items.detail: Head x4 (M4A1-S 3.475, Desert Eagle 3.9); chest x1, stomach x1.25, legs x0.75. Damage falls with range by the weapon range modifier per 500 units (AK-47 0.98, M4A1-S 0.94, MAC-10 0.80, UMP-45 0.75).

items.name: Armour
items.detail: Kevlar ($650) covers the body; the helmet (Kevlar and Helmet $1,000) covers the head. Armour penetration is half the armour ratio: AK-47 77.5 percent, M4s 70, AWP 97.5, Desert Eagle 93.2, Tec-9 90.6, Five-SeveN 91.2, USP-S 50.5, Glock-18 47.

items.name: One-tap facts (derived from game data)
items.detail: AK-47: one head hit kills through a helmet at normal ranges (about 112). M4A4 and M4A1-S: about 92 to a helmeted head, so two hits. Desert Eagle: one head hit through a helmet out to long range. USP-S (about 140) and Glock-18 (about 120) kill a helmetless head up close, the Glock only within about 500 units. AWP: any chest or stomach hit kills; a leg hit does not.

items.name: Tagging
items.detail: Being hit slows you down; the weapon you hold sets how much (shown as STOPPING POWER in the buy menu). Exact CS2 values were not found.

items.name: Penetration
items.detail: Rifles and the Desert Eagle have penetration power 2, AWP and SSG 08 2.5, pistols and SMGs 1 (Oct 2026 data), so rifles and snipers shoot through thin cover. Leetify says an average player gets at least one wallbang kill in about 40 percent of matches.

items.name: Reloads (March 2026 rework)
items.detail: A reload discards the bullets left in the magazine. Reserve per weapon: AK-47 3 magazines, M4A4 4, M4A1-S 3, AWP 2, Desert Eagle 3, USP-S 2, Glock-18 3. Attacks are blocked for about 2.5 s (AK-47) to 3.1 s (M4) after a reload starts. Since Sept 2026 holding the reload key gives a slower, silent reload.

items.name: Grenade prices and limits
items.detail: Flashbang $200, smoke $300, HE $300, molotov $400 (T), incendiary $500 (CT), decoy $50; limits 2 flashes and 4 grenades in total. All grenades drop on death in Competitive.

items.name: Grenade effects
items.detail: Smoke lasts roughly 18 to 20 s (guides differ). Fire deals about 40 HP per second: molotov about 7 s, incendiary about 5.5 s since May 2024. HE up to about 98 unarmoured, 57 armoured. Flash duration depends on angle and distance. Molotovs no longer break on players in flight (early 2026).

items.name: The bomb
items.detail: Bomb timer 40 s; defuse 10 s, or 5 s with a $400 kit. Explosion damage redesigned July 8 2026 (precomputed per map; no published values). Since July 20/21 2026 the explosion clears smoke and puts out fire nearby, and the health-bar damage preview appears once the bomb is audible. Plant time is about 3 s (unverified). A beta in October 2025 tested a defuse delay; no evidence it shipped.

items.name: Sound
items.detail: Running makes footsteps; walking and crouch-walking are silent, as are weapon switches. Jumps and landings make noise. Since Sept 2026 the held-key reload and unscoping are silent.

items.name: Sub-tick
items.detail: CS2 servers use sub-tick timing for inputs. Valve has made several fixes to movement and shot timing; guides say counter-strafing and peeker's advantage still work but feel different from CS:GO.

items.name: Start and cap
items.detail: $800 at the start of each half; $16,000 maximum (Oct 2026 config).

items.name: Round win
items.detail: $3,250 for elimination or time; $3,500 when the bomb explodes or is defused.

items.name: Loss bonus
items.detail: $1,400, then +$500 per consecutive loss, up to $3,400 ($1,400, $1,900, $2,400, $2,900, $3,400). Each half starts with one loss counted, so losing the pistol round pays $1,900. Most 2026 guides say a win lowers the count by one step rather than resetting it; some still describe a reset (unverified). The scoreboard tooltip shows your team's next loss income.

items.name: Objective money
items.detail: Planting player +$300; defusing player +$300. Ts who plant but lose the round get $600 extra each (cut from $800 in May 2024).

items.name: Kill rewards
items.detail: Default $300 (rifles, pistols, P90). SMGs $600 (MAC-10, MP9, MP7, MP5-SD, UMP-45, PP-Bizon). Nova, MAG-7, Sawed-Off $900; XM1014 $600. AWP $100. Zeus x27 $100. Knife $1,500. Casual pays 50 percent. Killing a teammate costs $300.

items.name: Pistol and SMG prices (Oct 2026)
items.detail: Pistols: Glock-18, USP-S, P2000 $200; P250 $300; Dual Berettas $300; Tec-9, Five-SeveN, CZ75-Auto $500; R8 $600; Desert Eagle $700. SMGs: MAC-10 $1,050; UMP-45 $1,200; MP9 $1,250; PP-Bizon $1,300; MP7, MP5-SD $1,400; P90 $2,350.

items.name: Gear prices
items.detail: Kevlar $650; Kevlar and Helmet $1,000; defuse kit $400 (CT); Zeus x27 $200.

items.name: Typical full buys
items.detail: T: AK-47, Kevlar and Helmet, smoke, two flashes, molotov = $4,800. CT: M4, Kevlar and Helmet, kit, smoke, two flashes, incendiary = $5,500. An AWP full buy costs about $1,850 to $2,050 more than the rifle version.

items.name: Buy types
items.detail: Full buy: rifle, armour and full utility. Eco (save): spend little or nothing to full buy next round. Force buy: spend everything on the best you can. Half buy: some gear while keeping enough for a full buy next round. Guides suggest a full eco below about $2,000 each after a loss and forcing around $2,500 to $3,500 before a bonus round; numbers differ between sources.

items.name: Pistol round and second round
items.detail: Pistol round: $800 each, usually Kevlar alone or a pistol upgrade plus a grenade. The pistol winners often anti-eco with SMGs for the $600 kill reward; the losers ($1,900 plus kill money) usually save or force.

items.name: Economy: round win rewards
items.detail: elimination: 3250. bombDefused: 3500. bombExploded: 3500. timeExpired: 3250. notes: Team income per player on the winning team. CTs win on time if no bomb is planted when the clock runs out.

items.name: Economy: loss bonus
items.detail: base: 1400. step: 500. max: 3400. ladder: 1400; 1900; 2400; 2900; 3400. startingLosses: 1. pistolRoundLoss: 1900. formula: Loss income = $1,400 + $500 x min(L, 4), where L is the team's loss counter before this loss. L starts at 1 (mp_starting_losses 1), goes up by 1 on each loss and goes down by 1 on each win..

items.name: Economy: loss bonus (2)
items.detail: cs2Rule: CS2 (mp_consecutive_loss_aversion 1): a round win steps the loss counter down by one instead of resetting it, so a team that wins one round after a losing streak still gets a high loss bonus if it loses again. CS:GO reset it to zero.. onWin: Counter minus 1 (not reset)..

items.name: Economy: loss bonus (3)
items.detail: resetAtHalf: Money resets to $800 at half-time; the counter is understood to return to its starting value (unverified).. readOnScreen: The Tab scoreboard shows a 'Loss Bonus' value with the tooltip '{team} will earn $X with a round loss'. Read it there instead of computing it.. consecutive_round_losses (available while playing)..

items.name: Economy: loss bonus (4)
items.detail: noIncomeOnTimeLoss: Terrorists still alive when they lose on time get no loss income (UI string: '+$0 penalty for running out of time').. unverified: true

items.name: Economy: plant bonus
items.detail: amount: 600. rule: If the bomb was planted but the Terrorists still lose the round, each Terrorist gets extra team income ('team income for planting the bomb'), on top of the loss bonus.. note: The shipped CS2 competitive cfg sets cash_team_planted_bomb_but_defused 600. Many older guides (CS:GO) say $800. Confirm with the in-game money notice.. unverified: true

items.name: Economy: per dead enemy team income
items.detail: amount: 50. rule: Since July 2025 a team income of $50 per enemy eliminated is shown at round end ('+$X team income for N eliminated terrorists/CTs'; convar cash_team_per_dead_enemy 50).. note: Coverage described it as a CT economy change; both team strings exist in the game files, so whether Terrorists also get it is unverified.. unverified: true

items.name: Economy: short handed bonus
items.detail: amount: 1000. rule: A team that has been a player short (for example after an abandon) for 2 rounds becomes eligible for +$1,000 short-handed team income (cash_team_bonus_shorthanded 1000, mp_shorthanded_cash_bonus_round_delay 2). Kicked players do not count.

items.name: Economy: personal objective rewards
items.detail: bombPlanted: 300. bombDefused: 300. teamKill: -300. killHostage: -1000

items.name: Economy: kill rewards
items.detail: group: Knife. amount: 1500; group: Shotguns: Nova, MAG-7, Sawed-Off. amount: 900; group: SMGs: MAC-10, MP9, MP7, MP5-SD, UMP-45, PP-Bizon; XM1014 shotgun. amount: 600; group: Rifles, pistols (incl. CZ75-Auto, Desert Eagle, R8), P90, SSG 08, autosnipers, M249, Negev, grenades. amount: 300; group: AWP and Zeus x27. amount: 100

items.name: Economy: kill reward notes
items.detail: Casual halves kill rewards (factor 0.5). Kill rewards are personal; round rewards are team income paid to each player.

items.name: Economy: overtime
items.detail: premier: At 12-12 Premier plays one overtime: 6 rounds (MR3, 3 per side), first to 4 overtime round wins. Everyone gets $10,000 at the start of each overtime half (mp_overtime_startmoney 10000). Only one overtime is played (mp_overtime_limit 1), so a further tie ends as a draw. Each team gets 1 extra timeout for overtime.. competitive: No overtime; 12-12 is a tie.. startMoney: 10000.

items.name: Economy: overtime (2)
items.detail: format: MR3. note: Sources disagree on whether Premier repeats overtime; the shipped Premier cfg limits it to one.

items.name: Economy: half switch
items.detail: Sides swap after round 12 (mp_halftime 1, mp_maxrounds 24). Money and weapons reset: everyone starts the second half with $800 and a pistol. Half-time lasts about 15 s.

items.name: Economy: equipment rules
items.detail: Drop a weapon for a teammate with the drop key (default G); a teammate can pick it up. ; Grenade limits in Competitive: 4 in total, up to 2 flashbangs, 1 of each other type. ; You can carry one primary, one pistol, a knife, grenades, a Zeus and (T) the C4.

items.name: Economy: full buy costs
items.detail: T_rifle: AK-47 $2,700 + Kevlar + Helmet $1,000 = $3,700; with smoke, 2 flashes and molotov about $4,800.. CT_rifle: M4A4 or M4A1-S $2,900 + Kevlar + Helmet $1,000 = $3,900; with kit and utility about $5,000 to $5,400.. AWP: AWP $4,750 + Kevlar + Helmet $1,000 = $5,750; with utility about $6,200 to $6,500.. note: Arithmetic from current prices.

items.name: Economy: buy rules
items.detail: name: Full buy threshold. ; name: Buy together. detail: Coaches teach the team to buy or save as one. ; name: Next-round check. detail: Before buying, add your money to the loss income you would get if you lose this round. ; name: Eco. ; name: Force buy. ; name: Second round after a pistol win. ; name: After losing the pistol round. ; name: Last round of a half.

items.name: Economy: buy rules (2)
items.detail: ; name: Save when the round is lost. ; name: Plant for money. ; name: Drop for teammates. ; name: Track the enemy economy. detail: Use the enemy loss bonus and kills to guess their next buy: after losing a pistol round they usually have about $1,900 to $2,700 each (loss income plus any kill rewards), which points to an eco or a light force.

items.name: Economy: buy rules note
items.detail: Buy rules are standard coaching practice; no external guide was fetched in this session, so phrasing is generic. Numbers come from the current price list.

items.name: Economy: other modes
items.detail: wingman: start: 800. max: 8000. winElimOrTime: 2750. winBombOrDefuse: 3000. lossBase: 2000. lossStep: 300. casual: start: 1000. max: 10000. winElimOrDefuse: 2700. winBomb: 2700. lossFlat: 2400. killRewardFactor: 0.5. freeArmour: Kevlar + Helmet. freeKits: all CTs. rush: start: 800. max: 10000. lossBase: 2100. lossStep: 750. perDeadEnemy: 50

items.name: Timing: round time
items.detail: seconds: 115. display: 1:55. convar: mp_roundtime 1.92 (minutes). modes: Premier and Competitive. Wingman 1:30, Casual 2:15 on bomb maps, Rush 0:40.

items.name: Timing: freeze time
items.detail: premierSeconds: 20. competitiveSeconds: 15. wingmanSeconds: 10. casualSeconds: 5. rushSeconds: 11. note: Premier value from gamemode_competitive_tmm.cfg.

items.name: Timing: buy time
items.detail: seconds: 20. note: Counts from the end of freeze time in Premier, Competitive and Wingman; Casual 45 s; Rush 15 s. You must be in your buy zone; the money panel shows a green cart icon there.

items.name: Timing: bomb timer
items.detail: seconds: 40. convar: mp_c4timer 40

items.name: Timing: defuse
items.detail: withoutKitSeconds: 10. withKitSeconds: 5. note: Defusing stops if you let go of the use key or are moved off the bomb.

items.name: Timing: plant
items.detail: seconds: about 3 (community figure 3.2 including the animation). note: The planter must stand inside a bombsite and stay still; moving or jumping cancels.. unverified: true

items.name: Timing: round end to next round
items.detail: seconds: 7. convar: mp_round_restart_delay 7

items.name: Timing: half time
items.detail: seconds: 15. convar: mp_halftime_duration 15

items.name: Timing: warmup
items.detail: seconds: 120. allConnectedSeconds: 15. note: Shipped Competitive cfg: warm-up up to 120 s, cut to 15 s once everyone has connected. Official servers may differ.. unverified: true

items.name: Timing: timeouts
items.detail: premier: 3 tactical timeouts of 30 s per team (cfg uses 31 s), plus 1 more when the match goes to overtime.. competitive: Shipped defaults: 1 tactical timeout per team of up to 60 s (not overridden in the client cfg; server cfg may differ).. technical: 1 technical timeout per team of 120 s (Premier, Competitive, Wingman).. unverified: true

items.name: Timing: c4 rules
items.detail: One Terrorist spawns with the C4; only Terrorists can pick it up. ; After planting, the round timer is replaced by a bomb icon at top centre; there is no countdown number on the HUD. bomb reads planted, defused or exploded while playing, but Valve adds a small random delay to the plant event so it cannot be used as an exact timer.

items.name: Timing: utility
items.detail: smoke: durationSeconds: about 18 (community; 18 to 20 quoted). note: Puts out fire; HE grenades and bullets can open gaps.. unverified: true. molotov: durationSeconds: 7. damagePerSecond: 40. spreadUnits: 150. airburstSeconds: 2. 5. damagePerSecond: 40. spreadUnits: 110. note: Spreads faster than the molotov (CS2 CT incendiary change)..

items.name: Timing: utility (2)
items.detail: flashbang: blindSeconds: up to about 5 at full blind (community). 6. unverified: true. 6. unverified: true. zeus: rechargeSeconds: 30

items.name: Timing: tick rate
items.detail: Official servers run 64 tick with sub-tick input.

items.name: Game State Integration
items.detail: Game State Integration (GSI) is Valve's built-in feature: the game reads cfg files named gamestate_integration_*.cfg at launch and HTTP-POSTs JSON game state to the uri in each file. Nothing reads game memory. While you play, it reports only your own state plus map and round info; all-player, position, grenade, bomb and countdown data arrive only when spectating, on GOTV or in demos.

items.name: Throwing: Three throw strengths
items.detail: Left-click throws at full strength, right-click lobs short, and both buttons give a medium throw. Since Dec 2023 a medium throw needs no delay, and since Feb 2024 holding both then releasing them close together gives a clean 50% throw.

items.name: Throwing: Throw speeds in CS:GO code
items.detail: All grenades share a base throw velocity of 750 in weapons.vdata. CS:GO code threw at 90% of that (675 units/s), right-click at 30% and medium at about 65%, and tilted the throw 10 degrees up when you looked level. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Throwing: Moving adds your speed
items.detail: Your own movement is added to the throw (in CS:GO code 1.25 times your velocity). Run-throws go furthest, walk-throws sit between, standing throws are shortest, and moving backwards shortens them. Jumping adds height. (Unverified: The 1.25 factor is from CS:GO code; the order of distances comes from guides.)

items.name: Throwing: Run- and walk-throw consistency
items.detail: A run-throw only repeats if you are at full speed, on the same line, when you release. Walk-throws are slower and easier to repeat. Learn each lineup with its exact movement.

items.name: Throwing: Jump-throw in CS2 needs no bind
items.detail: Hold the throw, press jump, then release: the game treats it as a jump-throw and plays a grunt to confirm. Since Aug 2024 binds that mix jump and attack are ignored by default (cl_allow_multi_input_binds is cheat-protected).

items.name: Throwing: Jump-throw window
items.detail: Valve has not published the timing window for a jump-throw. One guide says about 200 ms. Practise until the grunt plays every time. (Unverified: Single non-official source for the window length.)

items.name: Throwing: Jump-throw consistency and preview
items.detail: Since Nov 2024 the practice grenade camera shows the jump-throw result while jump is held. On 18 May 2026 Valve improved jump-throw consistency and the preview's accuracy.

items.name: Throwing: Sub-tick release
items.detail: CS2 records the moment you release inside the tick (sub-tick). Valve improved sub-tick timing of grenade throws in Nov 2023, so the exact release moment counts, not just the tick it fell in.

items.name: Throwing: Bounces and grenade clips
items.detail: Grenades bounce off walls and floors and lose speed. Valve adds smooth grenade clips to maps so bounces stay predictable. HE and flash burst on their timer, even mid-bounce; smoke and decoy wait until they stop.

items.name: Throwing: Molotov landing rule
items.detail: A molotov or incendiary bursts only on ground up to 30 degrees steep; walls bounce it. If it never lands it air-bursts after 2 s.

items.name: Throwing: Line-up reticle
items.detail: Hold a pulled pin and a line-up reticle with tick marks appears after a delay you set per grenade type (default 2 s, range 0 to 5). You can keep your normal crosshair with it. Since 30 Sep 2026 it also works in freeze time.

items.name: Throwing: No trajectory preview in live matches
items.detail: Live matches show no flight path. In Practice, Grenade Camera shows a picture-in-picture of the landing spot and a glowing trail. In Competitive, dead players and spectators see grenade trails for 4 s.

items.name: Throwing: Valve's map guides, part 1
items.detail: Valve's official map guides mark where to stand, where to aim and where the grenade lands, flag jump-throws, and count a success streak. A Train guide came first (Nov 2024).

items.name: Throwing: Valve's map guides, part 2
items.detail: On 18 Mar 2026 Valve added starter guides for all Active Duty maps and allowed limited guides in Competitive and Retakes: the first 5 rounds of each half, 30 nodes at most. Cache got its guide in Apr 2026.

items.name: Throwing: Slopes changed lineups (Apr 2026)
items.detail: Animgraph 2 (live from 20 Apr 2026) changed player height on sloped ground, so lineups thrown from slopes may land elsewhere. Valve adjusted its official guides on 24 Apr 2026.

items.name: Throwing: Throwing mistakes, part 1
items.detail: 1) Wrong stance: a crouched lineup thrown standing lands elsewhere. 2) Tiny movement at release. 3) The wrong click. 4) Old CS:GO lineups that no longer bloom the same way.

items.name: Throwing: Throwing mistakes, part 2
items.detail: 5) Relying on an old jump-throw bind, which official servers ignore by default. 6) Throwing as the round restarts: a restart still cancels a throw in progress. 7) Flat throws at a wall that bounce back.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Range falloff
items.detail: Damage is multiplied by the gun's range modifier to the power of (distance / 500 units). Values from weapons.vdata: AWP 0.99, AK-47 0.98, M4A4 0.97, M4A1-S 0.94, P90 0.86, UMP-45 0.75. 500 units is about 12.7 m.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Hit-group multipliers
items.detail: Head uses the gun's headshot multiplier: 4 for most guns, 3.475 for the M4A1-S and 3.9 for the Desert Eagle. Stomach x1.25. Chest and arms x1. Legs x0.75.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Armour formula
items.detail: On an armoured area, health takes damage x armour ratio / 2: AK-47 77.5%, M4A4 70%, AWP 97.5%, SG 553 100%. Armour points lose half of the blocked part. If armour runs out, more goes to health.

items.name: Guns, damage model: What armour covers
items.detail: Kevlar ($650) covers chest, stomach and arms. Kevlar and helmet ($1000) adds the head. Legs are never armoured. The buy menu rates each gun's armour penetration.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Helmets and rifles
items.detail: Worked from the formula and game values: an AK-47 headshot through a helmet does about 112 close and 103 at 2000 units, so one tap kills. An M4A4 or M4A1-S headshot does about 92 against a helmet (132 without), so it does not.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Helmets on pistol rounds
items.detail: Worked from the formula: a Glock headshot does 120 without a helmet but about 56 with one; a USP-S 140 against about 71. A helmet stops one-tap pistol kills, which is why CTs value it early.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Desert Eagle breakpoints
items.detail: Worked from the formula: a Deagle headshot through a helmet does about 193 close, 139 at 1000 units and about 101 at 2000, so it one-taps to long range. Body shots through Kevlar do about 49.

items.name: Guns, damage model: Friendly fire in Competitive
items.detail: Teammates take 33% of your bullet damage, 85% of your HE damage and 40% of other damage. Your own HE hurts you in full.

items.name: Guns, movement: Speed comes from the held gun
items.detail: Run speed in units/s from weapons.vdata: knife 250; Glock, USP-S, MP9 and MAC-10 240; Desert Eagle, SSG 08, P90 and UMP-45 230; M4A4 and M4A1-S 225; AK-47 and Galil 215; AWP 200, or 100 scoped.

items.name: Guns, movement: Walk and crouch speed
items.detail: In CS:GO code, walking (Shift) moves at 52% of run speed and crouching at 34%. CS2's counter-strafe detector uses 135.2 units/s as the move threshold, which is 52% of 260. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, movement: Accurate below about a third of max speed
items.detail: In CS:GO code there is no moving penalty below 34% of the gun's max speed, and the full penalty from 95%. The curve rises fast, so half speed already costs most of it. For the AK-47 the line is about 73 units/s. (Unverified: Formula from CS:GO code; CS2 guides repeat the 34% figure but Valve has not published it.)

items.name: Guns, movement: Walking is not accurate
items.detail: Shift-walking (52% speed) is above the 34% line, so shooting while walking with a rifle carries most of the moving penalty. Stop before you shoot. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, movement: Counter-strafing
items.detail: To stop fast, tap the opposite key, release both and shoot once stopped. CS2's own detector counts a perfect counter-strafe as one done within a single tick. Hardware that does it for you gets you kicked on Valve servers since Aug 2024.

items.name: Guns, movement: Standing versus crouching
items.detail: Crouching cuts inaccuracy by about a quarter for most rifles (AK-47 0.0064 to 0.0048) and speeds recovery (0.37 s to 0.31 s). Valve cut crouch accuracy for the MP9, MP5-SD and MP7 in Jan 2025.

items.name: Guns, movement: Jumping
items.detail: In the air every gun gets a large penalty: the AK-47's jump value is about 22 times its standing value. Valve cut the MP9's jump accuracy hard in Jul 2025. The SSG 08 is the exception.

items.name: Guns, movement: Worst at take-off, best at the top
items.detail: In CS:GO code the in-air penalty is largest as you leave the ground and smallest near the top of the jump, where vertical speed is low. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, movement: Landing
items.detail: Landing adds a short accuracy penalty and slows you. Since Jan 2026 jumps and landings no longer use stamina; the landing slow depends on landing time and how hard you land.

items.name: Guns, movement: Ladders and boosts
items.detail: Ladders add a large accuracy penalty. Since May 2026 a player standing on a stack of two or more players also gets the ladder penalty (weapon_accuracy_stack_boost_limit 2).

items.name: Guns, movement: First shot and recovery
items.detail: Each shot adds inaccuracy that fades. In CS:GO code the extra falls to a tenth within the gun's recovery time: AK-47 0.37 s standing and 0.31 s crouched; Desert Eagle 0.81 s and 0.45 s (weapons.vdata). (Unverified: Recovery times are CS2 game values; the 'falls to a tenth' rule is CS:GO code.)

items.name: Guns, movement: Tap, burst or spray by range
items.detail: Long range: single taps with time between. Medium: bursts of three to five. Close: spray and pull the pattern. Crouching steadies a long spray.

items.name: Guns, movement: The crosshair shows real spread (Sep 2026)
items.detail: Since 22 Sep 2026 the default crosshair is Dynamic Quad, which opens to the real spread and inaccuracy. Watch it close before you take the shot.

items.name: Guns, recoil: Fixed pattern plus random spread
items.detail: Each gun has a fixed recoil pattern built from its recoil seed and recoil angle and size values in weapons.vdata, so the spray shape repeats. On top, each bullet has random inaccuracy that grows the longer you fire.

items.name: Guns, recoil: Recoil reset
items.detail: In CS:GO code the recoil step falls to a tenth about 0.5 s after you stop firing. Leave about half a second between bursts to start again from the first bullet. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, recoil: Camera and bullets (Apr 2026)
items.detail: Since 21 Apr 2026 the camera kick from recoil matches CS:GO more closely while bullets keep CS2's pattern. Aim punch from being shot now shows in full on screen whatever your ping.

items.name: Guns, recoil: Follow Recoil crosshair
items.detail: The Follow Recoil option moves the crosshair with the gun's predicted recoil. It helps to learn a spray, since you can see where bullets are going.

items.name: Guns, recoil: Recent gun changes
items.detail: Jan 2025: FAMAS more accurate and $1,950; Jul 2025: MP9 more recoil; Jan 2026: MP7 and MP5-SD more damage and less falloff; Mar 2026: reloads discard the magazine; Apr 2026: burst delay bug fixed.

items.name: Guns, recoil: How to control a spray
items.detail: Pull down against the climb, then steer against each side swing. Start the pull with the second or third bullet, and stop or reset once the pattern turns wild.

items.name: Guns, recoil: About the spray notes
items.detail: The spray shapes below come from community guides. They agree on the climb but differ on bullet counts and on some side directions. Test each one in practice. (Unverified: Community guides only; they disagree on details.)

items.name: Guns, snipers: AWP basics
items.detail: $4,750, 115 damage, 5-round magazine, about 1.46 s between shots and a $100 kill reward. Two zoom levels, each taking 0.05 s. Moves at 200 units/s, 100 when scoped.

items.name: Guns, snipers: AWP needs the scope and a full stop
items.detail: Standing inaccuracy is 0.0808 unscoped against 0.002 scoped, about 40 times worse. The moving value (0.176) wipes out the scope's gain, so stop fully before you shoot.

items.name: Guns, snipers: AWP damage breakpoints
items.detail: Worked from the formula: 97.5% of 115 goes through Kevlar, so a chest, stomach or arm hit kills an armoured full-health player at any normal range. A leg hit (about 86) does not.

items.name: Guns, snipers: Quick-scope timing
items.detail: Zooming takes 0.05 s, but extra inaccuracy from the switch fades over the recovery time (AWP 0.35 s standing, 0.25 s crouched). Firing the instant the scope appears is less reliable. Stop, scope, settle briefly, fire. (Unverified: Valve publishes no quick-scope window; the settle advice comes from guides and CS:GO-style recovery.)

items.name: Guns, snipers: The scope shows inaccuracy (Oct 2025)
items.detail: Since Oct 2025 sniper scopes show current inaccuracy, so a wide, blurred scope means the shot is not ready. The option is on by default (cl_sniper_show_inaccuracy).

items.name: Guns, snipers: Unscope after the shot
items.detail: The AWP and SSG 08 unscope after each shot and re-zoom by default (cl_sniper_auto_rezoom). A setting can delay the unscope. Since Sep 2026 un-scoping is silent.

items.name: Guns, snipers: SSG 08
items.detail: $1,700, 88 damage, $300 reward, 230 units/s scoped or not. Its jump value is about 0.006 against the AWP's 0.134, so it stays accurate near the top of a jump. Liquipedia notes this is weaker than in older games.

items.name: Guns, snipers: SSG 08 damage
items.detail: Worked from the formula: a headshot does about 299 through a helmet, so it kills. An armoured chest shot does about 75, so follow up or switch.

items.name: Guns, snipers: Desert Eagle
items.detail: 53 damage, x3.9 headshot, 0.225 s between shots. Recovery is 0.81 s standing and 0.45 s crouched (weapons.vdata), so tap with pauses. Jumping makes it wildly inaccurate.

items.name: Guns, penetration: Penetration power by gun
items.detail: From weapons.vdata: 1.0 for pistols (except Deagle and R8), SMGs and shotguns; 2.0 for rifles, machine guns, Desert Eagle and R8; 2.5 for the AWP, SSG 08 and auto-snipers. The buy menu shows this as penetration power.

items.name: Guns, penetration: How walls cut damage, part 1
items.detail: In CS:GO code each surface costs about 16% of the bullet's current damage, plus a fixed chunk that is larger for low-power guns and hard materials. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, penetration: How walls cut damage, part 2
items.detail: Thick surfaces cost more, growing with the square of thickness. Objects thicker than 90 units stop the bullet, and it stops after 4 surfaces or under 1 damage. Wood crates, glass and grates are easy to shoot through. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, penetration: Practise wallbangs
items.detail: On a private server, sv_showimpacts 1 and sv_showimpacts_penetration 1 show where bullets hit and how much damage got through.

items.name: Guns, penetration: Recent penetration changes
items.detail: Valve reworked bullet penetration in Oct 2025 and fixed a regression. In May 2026 some Cache windows got grating that blocks bullets. The death event records how many objects a kill went through.

items.name: Guns, penetration: Smoke does not stop bullets
items.detail: Bullets pass through smoke, and the death event flags kills made through it. Spraying a smoke can hit players you cannot see.

items.name: Guns, tagging: What tagging is
items.detail: Getting hit slows you down. The buy menu calls this stat stopping power. Quick hits stack up to a cap.

items.name: Guns, tagging: Tagging values per gun
items.detail: First-hit and later-hit values in weapons.vdata: rifles 0.40 and 0.55 (M4A1-S 0.40 and 0.40); AWP and SSG 08 0.35 and 0.40; Desert Eagle 0.40 and 0.55; Glock, USP-S, Five-SeveN 0.50 and 0.65; SMGs 0 and 0; knife 0.30.

items.name: Guns, tagging: Lower means a harder slow
items.detail: The server scale mp_tagging_scale (1 by default) says lower values give greater tagging. The per-gun values work as speed multipliers too, so a gun with a low value slows the target more. (Unverified: The convar text covers the global scale; reading the per-gun values the same way relies on CS:GO code.)

items.name: Guns, tagging: How the slow is worked out
items.detail: In CS:GO code the victim's speed is multiplied by a value built from these numbers, scaled by the victim's own weapon and clamped between about 0.2 and 0.65. HE damage also slows, more for bigger hits. (Unverified: Value comes from CS:GO source code; CS2 has not published it, so it may differ.)

items.name: Guns, tagging: Tagging delay since Aug 2024
items.detail: Valve delays the slow by 2 ticks (sv_predictable_damage_tag_ticks 2) to stop players jumping back on screen. You keep full speed a fraction longer after a hit.

items.name: Guns, tagging: Coaching point
items.detail: Once hit you cannot strafe out at full speed. Commit to the duel or the nearest cover; do not wide-swing back out.

items.name: Roles
items.detail: Entry (first in, takes the first fight), support (utility for the entry, trades), lurker (plays away from the team to catch rotations), AWPer, anchor (CT who holds a site), rotator, in-game leader (IGL: calls buys and strategy). Roles overlap: an IGL can lurk, an AWPer can entry.
